title: Thinking Machines Lab Releases Inkling: A 975B-Parameter Open-Weights Multimodal MoE With 41B Active Parameters And Controllable Thinking Effort
summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, a 975B-parameter open-weights multimodal Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 41B active parameters, a 1M-token context window, and native text, image, and audio input.

title: Microsoft is reportedly training salespeople to talk down OpenAI and Anthropic
summary: Microsoft is reportedly training its salespeople to promote its in-house AI models as more efficient and cost-effective than those from competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: Firma prehnitá od základov, Apple si s OpenAI nedáva servítku. Čo pikantné sa píše v žalobe?
summary: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging theft of classified components for job interviews and data extraction from a former employee's storage.

title: Refusal Is Redundantly Distributed, Not Localized: A Per-Layer Ablation Study on Llama-3.1-8B
summary: A study on Llama-3.1-8B found that the refusal mechanism is redundantly distributed, rather than localized, replicating and extending findings that a single direction can causally ablate and steer model behavior.

title: Ant Group AI Strategy Tightens: Lingguang Retreats as A-Fu Takes Center Stage
summary: Ant Group is restructuring its AI strategy, shifting its Lingguang general model to exploration while making the health-focused A-Fu model its main strategic thrust, with 28.97M monthly active users targeting the medical vertical.

title: Alibaba Bets $10.6B on CXMT: The Strategy Behind China Largest Memory Maker IPO Support
summary: Alibaba is investing 7.6 billion RMB ($10.6B) in CXMT ChangXin Memory Technologies, becoming its largest industrial investor ahead of its 29.5 billion RMB IPO.

title: China First Full-Size Humanoid Autonomously Completes Long-Horizon Household Tasks Behind a Counter-Consensus Brain System
summary: The LimX Dynamics Oli humanoid robot autonomously completed long-horizon household tasks using its COSA 0.5 brain system, demonstrating a global second-level capability for humanoid robots.

title: Seven Phone Models Receive China AI Filing as Apple, Xiaomi, OPPO and Others Confirm On-Device LLM Compliance
summary: Seven phone models, including devices featuring Apple Intelligence, Alibaba Qwen, Xiaomi MiMo, and OPPO Andes, have received China AI filing for their on-device generative AI services, confirming compliance.

title: How AI is rewriting India’s credit story
summary: AI is transforming India's credit landscape by reducing borrower evaluation costs, enabling lenders to responsibly serve previously underserved customer segments.

title: India’s 132nd Unicorn, Groww’s Q1 Profit Run & More
summary: AI startup Emergent has achieved unicorn status, joining India's parade of rapidly growing companies after a significant funding round.

title: Baidu to power AI search for Apple’s Apple Intelligence in China
summary: Apple and Baidu are partnering to integrate Baidu's AI-powered search experience into Apple Intelligence for iPhone users in China, enhancing Siri and providing image and text understanding capabilities.

title: Alibaba and Baidu shares jump in Hong Kong on Apple AI partnership
summary: Shares of Alibaba and Baidu jumped in Hong Kong following the announcement of their AI partnership with Apple, intensifying the technological rivalry between China and the U.S.

title: Xiaomi introduces Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 for embodied AI and robot generation
summary: Xiaomi introduced Xiaomi-Robotics-U0, a 38-billion-parameter multimodal autoregressive foundation model for embodied AI and robot generation, unifying four core capabilities within a single framework.

title: Exclusive: AI Sales Intelligence Startup Reo.Dev Raises $11.3 Mn To Expand In US
summary: AI-powered sales intelligence startup Reo.Dev raised $11.3 million in a Series A funding round to expand its operations in the U.S.

title: OriginBlame: Record- and Token-Level Data Provenance for AI Training Datasets
summary: OriginBlame is a novel system for record- and token-level data provenance in AI training datasets, addressing the practical gap in locating specific training records for unlearning algorithms.

title: SPINE: Bridging the Cyber-Physical Gap with Agentic AI
summary: SPINE proposes an Agentic AI approach to bridge the cyber-physical gap in embodied AI, enabling more scalable deployment of foundation models into physical robot platforms.

title: Interventional Grounding Audits: Black-Box Premise-Dependency Tests for LLM Chain-of-Thought via Predicate Substitution
summary: This paper introduces interventional grounding audits, a black-box, step-level test using predicate substitution to evaluate the genuine premise-dependency in LLM chain-of-thought reasoning.

title: Probabilistic Extension of Neuro-Symbolic AGI Robots based on Belnap's Typed Intensional FOL
summary: This paper proposes a probabilistic extension of neuro-symbolic AGI robots based on Belnap's Typed Intensional FOL, aiming to combine neural learning and symbolic reasoning for enhanced cognitive power.

title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
summary: This survey examines self-improving autonomous agents, framing them as adaptive systems that convert experience into controllable evolution with minimal human input, moving from prototypes to deployed systems.

title: Improving Molecular Property Prediction in Small Language Models Using Graph-based Tools
summary: This research proposes a Context-Augmented Prompting framework to improve molecular property prediction in small language models, addressing their structural blindness with graph-based tools.

title: Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents
summary: This paper discusses Oracle Agent Memory as an enterprise memory substrate to address the system problem of long-horizon agents retaining task state, recovering user-specific facts, and accumulating procedural knowledge.

title: Learning Safe Agent Behaviour from Human Preferences and Justifications via World Models
summary: This research addresses safely training and deploying agent policies in safety-critical environments by learning safe agent behavior from human preferences and justifications via world models.

title: Networked Intelligence: Active Shared Context Graphs for Human-AI Team Science
summary: This paper introduces "Networked Intelligence" with Active Shared Context Graphs to enable collaborative Human-AI team science, moving beyond single-reasoner AI-for-science systems.

title: AI-Native Insurance for Agentic AI: Pricing, Underwriting, and End-to-End Automation
summary: This paper develops an AI-native mathematical framework for underwriting, pricing, and contract design of insurance for agentic AI, addressing challenges posed by autonomous AI systems.

title: Cost-Optimal Foundation Model Deployment Portfolio for Transportation Management
summary: This research explores a cost-optimal portfolio approach for deploying foundation models, including LLMs and VLMs, for various tasks in transportation management centers.

title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable
summary: This paper introduces the "Harness Handbook" to address the challenge of making evolving agent harnesses readable, navigable, and editable, as harnesses are crucial for agent capabilities.

title: Theory-Level Autoformalization: From Isolated Statements to Unified Formal Knowledge Bases
summary: This research focuses on theory-level autoformalization, aiming to translate natural language into unified formal, machine-verifiable knowledge bases, moving beyond isolated statements.

title: Set-shifting Behavioral Test for Harnessed Agents
summary: This paper introduces a set-shifting behavioral test and benchmark to study how LLM agents adapt their tool choices when the reliability of tools silently changes during a session.

title: LAPO: Leave-One-Turn Attribution for Self-Generated Process Rewards in Multi-Turn Search Reasoning
summary: This research proposes LAPO, a self-generated process-supervision method based on leave-one-turn attribution, to provide fine-grained rewards for multi-turn search reasoning in reinforcement learning.

title: How Far Can Root Cause Analysis Go on Real-World Telemetry Data?
summary: This paper investigates the extent of root cause analysis on real-world telemetry data for production microservice failures, assessing the effectiveness of classical and LLM-based approaches.

title: Multi-Agent Collaborative Reasoning with Tool-Augmented Evidence for Urban Region Profiling
summary: This research proposes using multi-agent collaborative reasoning with tool-augmented evidence to address the problem of urban region profiling in urban computing applications.

title: AI advice suppresses people's willingness to say "I don't know", even when the advice is wrong and accuracy is incentivized
summary: This study finds that AI advice suppresses people's willingness to admit uncertainty, even when the advice is incorrect and accuracy is incentivized, highlighting potential ethical concerns regarding over-reliance on AI.

title: SAFETY SENTRY: Context-Aware Human Intervention via EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE Routing
summary: SAFETY SENTRY proposes a context-aware human intervention method via EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE routing to safeguard LLM agents from misjudged actions that could cause irreversible harm in real-world environments.

title: Automatic Ordinary Differential Equations Discovery For Biological Systems Using Large Language Model Powered Agentic System
summary: This research explores automatic scientific discovery by using a large language model-powered agentic system to discover Ordinary Differential Equations for biological systems.

title: STOCKTAKE: Measuring the Gap Between Perception and Action in LLM Agents with a Fair Oracle
summary: STOCKTAKE introduces a method for measuring the perception-action gap in LLM agents during multi-week decision tasks, utilizing a fair oracle for improved evaluation.

title: UESF-Bench: Benchmarking and Probing for Unified Embodied Seeking and Following
summary: UESF-Bench is introduced as a new benchmark to evaluate embodied agents' unified seeking and following capabilities, addressing limitations in existing language-guided human following tasks.

title: Explaining Reinforcement Learning Agents via Inductive Logic Programming
summary: This research explores explaining Reinforcement Learning agents via Inductive Logic Programming to enhance transparency and interpretability, which is crucial for safety-critical and human-centric AI systems.

title: When Bots Join the Team: Bot Adoption and the Institutional Fabric of Open-Source Software Projects
summary: This research investigates the impact of AI agent adoption on the institutional fabric and organization of open-source software projects when bots join human development teams.

title: AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities
summary: AgentCompass is introduced as a unified evaluation infrastructure for autonomous agent capabilities, aiming to address fragmented evaluation pipelines and improve reproducibility.

title: CAVA: Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems
summary: This paper introduces CAVA, a framework for verifying and attesting runtime actions of agentic AI systems across diverse execution environments to ensure governance. It addresses the complexity of tracking and validating actions like publishing code or moving money performed by heterogeneous agent runtimes.

title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents
summary: This research introduces an "Experience Memory Graph" to enable LLM agents to perform one-shot error correction in complex, long-horizon tasks. This aims to help agents recover from compounding errors during autonomous decision-making.

title: AIMO Interpretability Challenge
summary: The AIMO Interpretability Challenge is proposed as a competition to evaluate mathematical language models by distinguishing robust from spurious reasoning based on their internal mechanisms. It addresses limitations of standard reasoning benchmarks that focus only on final answers.

title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
summary: HealthClaw is presented as an open-source, self-evolving agent architecture designed for longitudinal personal health management. It adapts support as a person's routines and health data change, separating shared safety rules from individual preferences.

title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling
summary: This paper presents an AI-accelerated, end-to-end framework designed to rapidly upskill professionals and address enterprise skills gaps. It aims to reduce the time required to close skill deficiencies.

title: Earthquaker-AI: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework with Rubric-Based Assessment for Primary School Earthquake Education
summary: Earthquaker-AI is introduced as a hybrid educational framework that integrates a conversational AI assistant based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a robotics project. It aims to enhance earthquake preparedness education for primary school students.

title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
summary: This paper proposes a "Deep Interaction" method for efficient human-AI interaction with large reasoning models, particularly focusing on improving error correction in Chain-of-Thought reasoning. It aims to address issues where current methods struggle to recover from LLM errors.

title: FixItFlow: Automated Troubleshooting Guide Generation from Cloud Incidents
summary: FixItFlow is presented as an automated system designed to generate troubleshooting guides from cloud incidents, addressing the labor-intensive and often outdated nature of manual guide creation. It aims to improve rapid diagnosis and resolution of cloud service issues.

title: Ask Before You Diagnose: Safe-Psych, a Sequential Evaluation Benchmark for LLMs in Psychiatry
summary: Safe-Psych is proposed as a sequential evaluation benchmark to assess Large Language Models (LLMs) in psychiatry, focusing on their ability to request clarification or abstain when information is insufficient. It addresses concerns about unsupported diagnoses in clinical decision support.

title: Designing Safety-Constrained LLM Systems for Public Health Information Access
summary: This paper describes the design and implementation of a safety-constrained Large Language Model (LLM) system for public health information access, specifically focusing on maternal and child health resource navigation. The goal is to provide flexible and natural interfaces while ensuring safety.

title: Safeguard-Conditioned Uplift: Measuring Utility-Risk Frontiers for Dual-Use Biology Assistants
summary: This research proposes a method for measuring the utility-risk frontier of dual-use biology assistants by evaluating how access conditions change benign utility and harmful actionable assistance. It aims to go beyond standard safety metrics like refusal behavior or jailbreak success.

title: Final Authority in AI Governance: Frontier-Provider Sovereignty and Action-Centered Deployer Governance
summary: This paper examines two governance models for AI systems embedded in organizational workflows: frontier-provider sovereignty and action-centered deployer governance. It debates where final authority should reside in AI governance structures.

title: LessonBench-V1: A Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating AI Lesson Generation Agents
summary: LessonBench-V1 is introduced as a new benchmark dataset for systematically evaluating AI lesson generation agents. Comprising 647 human-written lessons paired with LLM-based reviews, it aims to standardize the assessment of educational content generation systems.

title: Beyond Backbone Backpropagation: A Decoupled Strategy for Efficient Transfer Learning
summary: This paper proposes a decoupled strategy for efficient transfer learning in deep learning models, aiming to reduce computational costs and energy demands. The method adapts normalization layers and separates feature extraction from classifier training.

title: The Perplexity Trap: When Patent Law Makes Human Writing Look Like AI
summary: This article discusses how European Patent Office (EPO) guidelines hold applicants responsible for LLM-assisted content, creating challenges in distinguishing human from AI-generated patent text. It highlights the difficulties due to current AI detection limitations.

title: Federated Explainable Artificial Intelligence: Roles, Architectures, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of Federated Explainable Artificial Intelligence (F-XAI), addressing its roles, architectures, evaluation methods, and challenges. It explores how to achieve privacy-preserving collaborative model training while ensuring model interpretability.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Sequential Decision Rules for Event-Triggered LLM Invocation in Streaming Systems
summary: This research proposes uncertainty-aware sequential decision rules for event-triggered LLM invocation in streaming systems, aiming to optimize the use of costly LLMs. It frames the problem as a risk-based sequential stopping problem to decide when to switch from lightweight models to LLMs.

title: Autonomous UAV Route Planning for Coverage Maximization in Environmental Monitoring: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: This systematic literature review focuses on autonomous UAV route planning methods designed to maximize coverage in environmental monitoring applications. It considers energy limits, operational constraints, and geometric complexity.

title: Compaction as Epistemic Failure: How Agentic LLM Tools Fabricate Confirmed Results from Killed Processes
summary: This paper documents a failure mode in agentic LLM coding tools where compaction summaries incorrectly record partial output from timed-out commands as confirmed results. This "epistemic failure" affects the reliability of subsequent agent sessions.

title: HRO: Hierarchical Room-to-Object Framework for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation with Large Language Models
summary: HRO is a hierarchical room-to-object framework for zero-shot object goal navigation, enabling intelligent agents to explore and navigate to objects in unfamiliar environments using Large Language Models' prior knowledge. It aims to improve agent performance in novel navigation tasks.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture
summary: This paper discusses how large language models (LLMs) might produce homogeneous outputs, raising concerns that AI coding assistants could lead to a "monoculture" in software development. It explores whether this theoretical concern holds true in practice, considering how developers interact with models.

title: Operational Evidence Gaps for LLMs in Fraud Detection and Trust-and-Safety Workflows
summary: This article identifies a gap in operational evidence for using large language models (LLMs) in fraud detection and trust-and-safety workflows. It notes that while LLMs are proposed for these applications, their behavior as components within operational pipelines is often not fully evaluated in existing literature.

title: Inference Economics of Enterprise Coding Agents: A Case Study of Cloud vs. On-Premise LLMs
summary: This study examines the inference economics of enterprise coding agents, comparing the trade-offs between using API-based cloud frontier models and on-premise quantized open-weight models. It analyzes the costs, reasoning capabilities, and data sovereignty implications for engineering organizations.

title: SingGuard-NSFA: Extensible Guardrails for Agentic AI via Generative Reasoning and Real-Time Classification
summary: This paper introduces SingGuard-NSFA, an extensible guardrail framework designed to secure agentic AI systems against operational threats like prompt injection and dangerous tool misuse. The framework utilizes generative reasoning and real-time classification to enhance safety.

title: Baselines Before Architecture: Evaluating Coding Agents for Autonomous Penetration Testing
summary: This research emphasizes the importance of establishing baselines for evaluating coding agents used in autonomous penetration testing. It highlights the challenge of discerning performance improvements when systems simultaneously alter both their architecture and underlying large language models.

title: Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules: A Closed-Loop Framework
summary: This paper presents a closed-loop framework enabling LLM-based coding agents to self-improve by accumulating behavioral rules from human review feedback. This mechanism allows agents to retain corrections, preventing the repetition of past mistakes across sessions.

title: Efficient and Privacy Aware Edge Cloud Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models
summary: This paper explores efficient and privacy-aware edge-cloud collaborative inference for large language models, addressing challenges like latency, limited hardware, and user privacy on edge devices. It contrasts full cloud and standalone on-device inference, proposing a hybrid solution.

title: Analyzing Curricular Pattern Complexity Using AI to Improve On-Time Graduation Rates
summary: This work utilizes artificial intelligence techniques to analyze and revise complex curricular patterns in undergraduate degree programs. The goal is to improve on-time graduation rates by making previously labor-intensive data analysis tasks more efficient.

title: Full-Pipeline Inference Optimization for MiMo-V2.5 Series: Pushing Hybrid SWA Efficiency to the Limit
summary: This paper presents full-pipeline inference optimization techniques for the MiMo-V2.5 model family, focusing on enhancing efficiency. It details how Hybrid Sliding Window Attention, sparse Mixture-of-Experts, and multimodal encoders are combined to reduce attention compute and KVCache storage.

title: WaterMoE: Expert-Routing-based Watermarking for High Fidelity and Efficiency
summary: This paper introduces WaterMoE, an expert-routing-based watermarking technique designed for large language models (LLMs) to ensure high fidelity and efficiency. It aims to address concerns about content provenance and misuse, which have limited the practical adoption of previous watermarking methods.

title: Automatic Differentiation from Scratch: How PyTorch Computes Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: This paper details how PyTorch's automatic differentiation engine computes gradients for Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) training, providing explicit numerical values. It clarifies the two levels of differentiation required in this setting.

title: What Your Model Threw Away and Why You'll Want It Back: Masking, Fingerprinting, and Privacy from Discarded Geometry
summary: This paper develops a framework to analyze information discarded by machine learning models whose inputs are subject to a Lie group action. It explores how this discarded "geometry" relates to masking, fingerprinting, and privacy.

title: Targeted Recovery of Weight-Space Mechanisms From Neural Networks
summary: This paper proposes targeted parameter decomposition (tPD) as a method to recover interpretable weight-space mechanisms from neural networks. This approach aims to make large models more understandable by breaking them into computational components, addressing the high computational cost of traditional parameter decomposition.

title: TSSM: Triaxial State Space Model for Global Station Weather Forecasting with Temporal-Variable-Historical Modeling
summary: This paper introduces TSSM, a Triaxial State Space Model for Global Station Weather Forecasting that incorporates temporal-variable-historical modeling. This new approach aims to improve accuracy in localized and extreme weather prediction, addressing limitations of existing methods.

title: Disentangling Knowledge States with Ability and Proficiency Modeling for Knowledge Tracing
summary: This paper proposes a new method for knowledge tracing (KT) that disentangles students' knowledge states using ability and proficiency modeling. The approach aims to improve the prediction of future student performance by accounting for the phase-specific nature of learning behaviors.

title: A Hybrid Mamba for Audio-Visual Navigation
summary: This paper introduces a Hybrid Mamba architecture for audio-visual navigation, aiming to update the fundamental backbone networks in this field. It addresses the inadequacy of long-standing convolutional and recurrent network paradigms for efficient representation.

title: CoDiffGRN: Rethinking Gene Regulatory Network Inference via the BEELINE-KGC Benchmark and Co-evolutionary Discrete Diffusion
summary: This paper introduces CoDiffGRN, a new method for inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell transcriptomic data using co-evolutionary discrete diffusion. The approach is evaluated against the BEELINE-KGC benchmark, addressing misalignments of existing methods with real-world biological needs.

title: ShortOPD: Recovering Pruned LLMs with Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper introduces ShortOPD, a method using Short-to-Long On-Policy Distillation to recover the performance of pruned large language models (LLMs). It aims to address the issue of pruned LLMs collapsing on free-form generation tasks despite being validated on multiple-choice recognition.

title: SteinGate: Tail-Sensitive Safe Reinforcement Learning via Stein Discrepancy
summary: This paper introduces SteinGate, a new approach for tail-sensitive safe reinforcement learning that uses a boundary-aware distributional safety certificate based on Stein Discrepancy. It aims to overcome limitations of traditional safe RL methods that often fail to detect rare but catastrophic tail events.

title: Concurrent Image Understanding and Generation: Self-Correcting Coupled Markov Jump Processes
summary: This paper explores concurrent image understanding and generation in artificial systems using self-correcting coupled Markov Jump Processes. It proposes integrating understanding and generation, similar to human cognition, leveraging Masked Diffusion Models.

title: EMAGN: Efficient Multi-Attention Graph Network via Learned Clustering for Scalable Traffic Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces EMAGN, an Efficient Multi-Attention Graph Network that uses learned clustering to improve scalability in traffic forecasting by modeling complex spatiotemporal dependencies.

title: Reassessing Muon for Matrix Factorization
summary: This research re-evaluates Muon, an optimizer for large-scale deep learning, finding it outperforms Adam and AdamW in large language model training by reshaping gradient updates through approximate orthogonalization.

title: Deconstructing Actor-Critic: A Large-scale Empirical Study of Design Components for Practitioners
summary: This empirical study deconstructs Actor-Critic reinforcement learning algorithms, examining their design components to improve reliability and reduce tuning budgets for real-world control systems.

title: Tabular Foundation Models for Discrete Choice Estimation
summary: This paper investigates the application of tabular foundation models (TFMs) for discrete choice estimation in marketing and operations, evaluating their effectiveness without task-specific estimation.

title: Accuracy-Preserving Stability Regularization for Large-Scale Retail Demand Forecasting
summary: This research proposes a training-time penalty, Accuracy-Preserving Stability Regularization, to constrain abrupt forecast movements and improve the stability and accuracy of large-scale retail demand forecasts.

title: Agora: Collective and Permissionless Internet-Scale Pretraining of Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Agora, a method for collective and permissionless internet-scale pretraining of large language models, overcoming datacenter limitations for multi-billion to trillion parameter models.

title: Where Should RL Post-Training Compute Go? Model Size, Search, Learning, and Feedback
summary: This study explores how to optimally allocate compute resources during reinforcement learning (RL) post-training for foundation models used in reasoning, planning, and robot-learning pipelines.

title: Self-Improving is Often Sudden: Enlightenment-style Finetuning for Large-Scale Models
summary: This research explores an 'enlightenment-style' finetuning phenomenon in large-scale models, hypothesizing that self-improvement often occurs suddenly, similar to human 'aha moments'.

title: EXPLORE: Exploration with Guided Search for Analog Topology Generation using Language Models
summary: This paper presents EXPLORE, a method using pretrained language models with guided search and sequence-to-sequence fine-tuning to automate analog circuit topology generation.

title: OrDA: Orthogonal Disentanglement of Access Habits Framework for Homepage Marketing Block Recommendations
summary: This paper proposes OrDA, an Orthogonal Disentanglement of Access Habits Framework, to improve homepage marketing block recommendations by separating content interest from habitual clicks, reducing bias.

title: Temperature Scaling Is Not Enough: Calibration Gaps Under Human Label Distributions
summary: This study argues that temperature scaling is insufficient for calibration in deep learning, highlighting calibration gaps when ground-truth labels are soft, crowd-sourced, or non-deterministic.

title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of LLMs via Attention Head Reweighting
summary: This research introduces Attention Head Reweighting as a parameter-efficient adaptation method to improve data-efficient learning for large language models (LLMs) in domains with scarce labeled data.

title: PUe: Biased Positive-Unlabeled Learning Enhancement by Causal Inference
summary: This paper introduces PUe, a Positive-Unlabeled learning enhancement method that uses causal inference to improve binary classification accuracy when only limited positive examples are labeled.

title: Discrete Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework from Tokenization to Generation
summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for discrete denoising diffusion models (DDMs), offering a compelling alternative to autoregressive modeling for parallel generation and iterative global refinement of discrete data.

title: Local Redundancy: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Plasticity from Synthetic Memorization
summary: This paper introduces Local Redundancy, an information-theoretic measure of neural network plasticity, which aims to better correlate with performance in continual and transfer learning than existing metrics.

title: PQFA: Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation of Fused Representations for Multimodal Classification
summary: This paper proposes PQFA, a Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation framework, a hybrid quantum-classical method that enhances fused representations using shallow variational quantum circuits for multimodal classification.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Anomaly Detection in Banking Transactions: An Internal Audit Perspective
summary: This paper examines the application of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for anomaly detection in banking transactions, focusing on its utility for internal audit and compliance in combating fraud.

title: DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers
summary: This paper introduces DeepLoop, a method for depth scaling in Looped Transformers that applies a compact stack of physical blocks multiple times to increase unrolled depth without increasing stored parameters.

title: A VAE-Driven Multi-Task Satellite-Aided Semantic Communication Framework for 6G-Enabled Connected Autonomous Vehicles
summary: This paper proposes a VAE-driven multi-task satellite-aided semantic communication framework for 6G-enabled Connected Autonomous Vehicles, aiming for bandwidth-efficient, reliable, and low-latency communication.

title: Factorized Spectral Representations for Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper presents Factorized Spectral Representations, a method for learning compact world models from interaction data to achieve sample-efficient deep reinforcement learning by viewing the transition kernel spectrally.

title: ExTernD: Expanded-Rank Ternary Decomposition Ternary LLM PTQ with Accuracy Approaching Any Quantization Level
summary: This paper introduces ExTernD, a post-training quantization method for LLMs that uses expanded-rank ternary decomposition to factorize weight matrices. This technique aims to maintain high accuracy while making LLMs more efficient.

title: Structured Reinforcement Learning for Bayesian Persuasion : Application to Intelligent Interactive Driving
summary: This paper introduces a structured reinforcement learning method for Bayesian persuasion, applying it to intelligent interactive driving to coordinate route choices of connected vehicles for dynamic traffic management.

title: Gauge-Invariant, Parameter-Insensitive Regularization for Potential Recovery from Flow on Directed Graphs
summary: This paper proposes a gauge-invariant, parameter-insensitive regularization method for recovering a latent potential from observed flow on directed graphs, addressing issues with standard regularization techniques.

title: The SIGReg Objective as Variational Free Energy: A Theoretical Active-Inference Account of JEPA World Models
summary: This paper provides a theoretical active-inference account of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) world models, showing how the choice of anti-collapse regularizer determines their training objective as variational free energy.

title: FastCentNN: Accelerating Centroid Neural Network with Entropy Proxy
summary: This report proposes FastCentNN, an accelerated variant of the Centroid Neural Network, which is an unsupervised competitive learning algorithm. It aims to reduce prolonged low-movement training phases by using an entropy proxy.

title: How the Hessian-Spectrum of Neural Networks Depends on Data
summary: This paper investigates how the Hessian-spectrum of neural networks depends on data, exploring its role in understanding the loss landscape, optimization dynamics, and generalization in deep learning.

title: Consensus as Privileged Context for Label-Free Self-Distillation
summary: This paper proposes using "Consensus as Privileged Context" for label-free self-distillation, a method to improve the reasoning accuracy of large language models by converting consensus signals into training supervision.

title: The Hyperspherical Geometry of CLIP Latent Space: A Semantic Mixture Model
summary: This paper analyzes the hyperspherical geometry of CLIP's latent space, which is governed by cosine similarity, and proposes a semantic mixture model to better capture its directional nature.

title: Conditional Invertible Neural Networks for Data-Driven UAV Control: A 2-D Proof of Concept
summary: This paper investigates conditional invertible neural networks (cINNs) as probabilistic inverse-dynamics models for data-driven control of multirotor UAVs, demonstrating a 2-D proof of concept.

title: DAGR: State-Conditioned Goal Representations via Difference-Aware Goal Cross-Attention
summary: This paper introduces DAGR (Difference-Aware Goal Cross-Attention), a new method for state-conditioned goal representations in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning, addressing the limitation of state-independent goal embeddings.

title: Constraint-Driven Model Optimization: An Industry Framework for Selecting Compression and Acceleration Techniques in Modern Machine Learning Systems
summary: This paper presents an industry framework for constraint-driven model optimization, guiding the selection of compression and acceleration techniques like quantization and pruning for modern machine learning systems.

title: Implementations of Quantum and Classical Topology-Aligned Architectures for Molecular Property Prediction
summary: This paper proposes quantum and classical topology-aligned architectures for molecular property prediction, designed for parameter-efficient learning in low-data, resource-constrained quantum chemistry regimes.

title: Algebraic Representability as the Limiting Regime of Grokking: An Exactly Solvable Model with Holomorphic Activations
summary: This paper investigates the phenomenon of grokking in neural networks, proposing algebraic representability as its limiting regime and studying it using an exactly solvable model with holomorphic activations.

title: MxGPS: Multiplex Graph Transformers for a Power Grid Foundation Model
summary: This paper introduces MxGPS, a Multiplex Graph Transformer architecture designed to create a Power Grid Foundation Model that mitigates topology overfitting encountered in single-task fine-tuning of GNNs.

title: A better way to turn 2D designs into 3D models for rapid prototyping
summary: Researchers developed an automated framework that enhances AI models' ability to generate CAD programs more accurately and efficiently, facilitating the conversion of 2D designs into 3D models for rapid prototyping.

title: Applied Computing wants to give oil and gas operators an AI model for the entire plant
summary: Applied Computing has raised a $20M Series A funding round to develop a foundation AI model tailored for the entire oil, gas, and petrochemical industry.

title: C-Norm: Cell-Distribution Normalization Enables Precision Recognition of Medical-Cell Image
summary: C-Norm is a cell-distribution normalization method designed to enhance the precision recognition of medical-cell images in AI detection models, particularly for ThinPrep Cytologic Test (TCT).

title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open-Source Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
summary: Boogu-Image-0.1 is an open-source, unified multimodal understanding and generation model family, including Base, Turbo, Edit, and Edit-Turbo variants, offering competitive performance in various tasks.

title: A Masked Autoencoder Approach to Unsupervised Steel Surface Defect Recognition
summary: This paper proposes a Masked Autoencoder approach for unsupervised steel surface defect recognition, leveraging self-supervised methods to learn useful representations from unlabeled surface images.

title: Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning: Pretrain-Finetuning or Joint Training?
summary: This research investigates self-supervised visual representation learning, comparing the efficacy of two primary approaches: a two-stage pretraining and finetuning pipeline versus a joint training method.

title: Continuously Evolving Deepfake Detection: An Architecture and Public-Benchmark Evaluation of a Dynamic Detection System
summary: This paper introduces a continuously evolving architecture for deepfake detection systems, addressing the performance gap between academic benchmarks and real-world content through a dynamic detection system.

title: Active Learning for Efficient Annotation of Surgical Videos with Weak Supervision
summary: This research proposes a human-in-the-loop framework combining active learning and dual-loss optimization to efficiently annotate surgical videos, reducing the expert effort required for spatial-temporal labeling.

title: Just-In-Time Scene Graph Growth: Combating Perceptual Saturation in Long-Horizon Robotics
summary: This research proposes a "Just-In-Time Scene Graph Growth" method to combat perceptual saturation in long-horizon robotics by addressing real-time, low-latency demands of 3D Scene Graphs for embodied agents.

title: AffectFlow-DINO: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Task Affect Estimation via Conditional Rectified Flow
summary: AffectFlow-DINO is a multi-task learning system that extends a deterministic architecture with a conditional rectified-flow head to perform uncertainty-aware affect estimation of in-the-wild facial behavior.

title: FOLIO: Focused Semantic Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
summary: FOLIO is proposed as a focused semantic memory system for online streaming video understanding, designed to continuously compress and retain information from observed video prefixes for unbounded streams.

title: Improving Medical Image Generative Models with Fr\'echet Distance Loss
summary: This research aims to improve diffusion generative models for synthetic medical image generation by addressing their limitations in capturing complex tumor morphology, potentially using Fréchet Distance Loss.

title: Accuracy Without Grounding: Diagnosing Visual Dependency Dissociation in Video LLM Benchmarks
summary: This research audits the assumption of visual understanding from benchmark accuracy in video LLMs, introducing the Visual Dependency Gap (VDG) to diagnose visual dependency dissociation across various models and architectures.

title: Reflecting Process Expertise in Procedural Material Generation
summary: This research focuses on reflecting process expertise in procedural material generation to achieve high-quality results in digital content creation, visual effects, and 3D asset design.

title: SARFA: Segment Anything with Radiomic Feature Alignment
summary: SARFA (Segment Anything with Radiomic Feature Alignment) is a proposed method to improve the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for medical imaging, addressing its struggles with ambiguous target segmentation in areas like tumor delineation.

title: Delving into the Temporal Challenges of Unified Video Protection Against Image-to-Video and Fine-Tuning-based Customization
summary: This research delves into temporal challenges for unified video protection against high-quality personalized video customization enabled by diffusion-based and image-to-video generation models, addressing related concerns.

title: Marker-free deformable registration and fusion for augmented reality-guided positive margin localization during tumor resection surgery
summary: This research proposes a marker-free deformable registration and fusion method for augmented reality-guided localization of positive margins during tumor resection surgery, aiming to improve surgical precision.

title: Detector Confidence Signals Presence Rather Than Occlusion in Cluttered Manipulation
summary: This research finds that an open-vocabulary object detector's confidence signals object presence rather than occlusion, often remaining high or even rising in cluttered manipulation scenarios, leading to misinterpretations.

title: DiffGI: Differentiable Geometry Images for High-Fidelity Thin-Shell 3D Generation
summary: DiffGI introduces Differentiable Geometry Images for high-fidelity thin-shell 3D generation, providing a surface-centric alternative to volumetric representations that struggle with non-manifold geometries like garments.

title: RoughNet: Mapping Arctic Sea Ice Roughness Using Diffusion-Based Super-Resolution of Satellite Imagery
summary: RoughNet is a proposed method that uses diffusion-based super-resolution of satellite imagery to accurately map Arctic sea ice roughness, addressing limitations of existing costly survey methods for climate modeling.

title: FM$^2$: Unified Federated Foundation Models for Heterogeneous Multimodal Medical Imaging
summary: FM$^2$ introduces Unified Federated Foundation Models for heterogeneous multimodal medical imaging, addressing data privacy concerns by enabling model training across institutions without centralizing sensitive data.

title: MultiAnimate: A Unified Framework for Controllable Multi-Character Animation
summary: MultiAnimate is a unified framework designed for controllable multi-character animation, addressing limitations of existing generative models that primarily focus on single-character animation.

title: ScanFocus: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
summary: ScanFocus is a coarse-to-fine framework for Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG), designed to retrieve specific object trajectories from video streams based on natural language expressions while balancing context modeling and precise localization.

title: CLIP-Guided Label-Free Discriminative Region Scoring for Fine-Grained Classification
summary: This research explores CLIP-guided label-free discriminative region scoring for fine-grained classification, leveraging vision models like CLIP and SAM for training-free segmentation and semantic encoding.

title: DreamSat-Pose: Spacecraft Pose Estimation from Single-View 3D Reconstructions and Learned 2D-3D Feature Matching
summary: DreamSat-Pose is a novel framework for spacecraft pose estimation that uses single-view 3D reconstructions and learned 2D-3D feature matching to determine 6-DoF pose for autonomous rendezvous operations.

title: GeoAnchor: Collaborative Reasoning via Latent Decomposition for 3D Spatial Understanding
summary: GeoAnchor proposes a collaborative reasoning framework using latent decomposition to improve multimodal large language models' understanding of 3D spatial relationships derived from 2D images.

title: TreeSRNF: Square-Root Normal Fields for Generative Modelling of the Geometric and Structural Variability in Tree-like 3D Objects
summary: TreeSRNF introduces a novel mathematical framework using Square-Root Normal Fields for generative modeling, enabling the analysis and creation of complex tree-shaped 3D objects with geometric and structural variability.

title: 2D Rotary Position Embedding for Scene Text Recognition with Transformers
summary: This paper proposes a 2D rotary position embedding for Transformers to improve Scene Text Recognition (STR) by better handling the 2D spatial structure of text.

summary: This paper presents GPOcc++, a method for unified sparse Gaussian occupancy prediction using visual geometry priors, aiming to improve 3D scene understanding crucial for embodied intelligence and autonomous driving.

title: M2P-AD: Memory-to-Prototype Learning with Boundary-aware Score Refinement for 3D Anomaly Detection
summary: This paper introduces M2P-AD, a memory-to-prototype learning method with boundary-aware score refinement to improve 3D anomaly detection by addressing excessive anomaly responses and false positives.

summary: This research proposes an attention-free and lightweight token reduction method to improve the efficiency of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), making them more deployable on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: GHR-VLM: Making Zero-Shot Transit Video Analytics Realizable with Grounded Hybrid Reasoning

title: UniPhysGen: Unified Physical Grounding for Simulation-Ready 3D Assets
summary: UniPhysGen provides a method for unified physical grounding for 3D assets, endowing them with articulation semantics and intrinsic physical properties required for realistic interaction in embodied AI and robotic simulations.

title: Human4K: A Large-Scale 4K Multi-View Mocap Dataset for Whole-Body 3D Human Reconstruction

title: Beyond Color Geometry: Evaluating Human-Like Color Representations in Vision Models

title: Exploratory, Communicative, and Deployable: Vision-Driven Embodied Agents for Open-World Mobile Manipulation

title: Learning Speaker Identity Beyond Language and Modality Constraints: Insights from the POLY-SIM 2026 Challenge

title: GPUSimBench: Towards Scalable and Reliable GPU-Accelerated Simulators in Embodied AI

title: A Bayesian framework for the uncanny valley in humanoid robot design

title: A 3DGS-Driven Dynamic Viewpoint and Vibrotactile Framework for Subsea Teleoperation Validated via fNIRS

title:
Competitive AI Safety is
the loss function to make sure AI goes well
summary: TLDR: AI safety needs a loss function and Competitive AI safety can deliver it. The development of AI safety research and tooling is currently diffuse. Lots of researchers, lots of models, lots of techniques. Lots of work that doesn't compound. In the past, diffuse work across an industry fell short by orders of magnitude to focussed, compounding work. It's time for our researchers to have more impact by following a loss function to 'code the perimeter' in AI safety. Competitive AI Safety's scope expands beyond safety benchmarks and a leaderboard. It will help the field deliver shared safety tools and interfaces and allow new and experienced practitioners to optimise solutions against a shared, measurable metric. I explored this pattern as part of a 30 hour BlueDot Technical AI Safety Project Sprint. The result was seq2feature : a Gemma-9B layer 20 SAE distilled into a 5.3MB probe that predicts latents from text alone: without reading a single activation . The probe's top-5 predictions actually fired in the SAE 95% of the time. By evaluating seq2feature over thousands of text examples per latent it could distinguish the spans where a latent would fire or not in the SAE 90% of the time. Beat that! It runs on a CPU and fails legibly when used out of distribution. The repo includes the probe, the held-out split, a UI and sentry framework and most importantly: the leaderboard . LLMs are not embodied and need to emit tokens to execute code or call tools before they can take actions in the world. A cheap text-only monitor can audit proposed LLM actions before they take place. Local coding agents can be summoned when the probe detects a harmful latent in an agent trace. Connecting the probe, a local coding agent and an AI safety researcher through a shared UI is one of the key ways we can tighten feedback loops in the field. This post is divided into three sections. Paradigm: Part one introduces Competitive AI Safety. Case study: Part two is my application of Competitive AI safety principles and the development of a text to label probe, seq2feature, distilled from an SAE and optimised to minimise its size. Full code here https://github.com/patrickod32/seq2feature Deployment Pattern: Part three outlines the three roles of local coding agents in AI Safety; Writing code, collaborating via shared UI with a safety researcher, and as part of a scalable LLM monitor. Section 1: Competitive AI safety OpenAI recently conducted a Parameter Golf challenge to attract model training talent. They invited AI developers to train the smartest (measured using FineWeb bits per byte) 16MB LLM in 10 minutes. Contestants tried every machine learning trick they could imagine on this measurable, tractable goal. Google's Neel Nanda has suggested that AI safety as a field should work on tractable interpretability problems, as introduced in his paradigm of Pragmatic Interpretability . I see an opportunity. As a former nanotech physicist and current AI architect I have expertise in the full AI stack: from semiconductor physics and wet lab nanolithography to financial compliance for AI agents and mechanistic interpretability. I wanted to work in a more targeted way on AI Safety and so I joined the BlueDot Technical AI Safety Project Sprint . This post and the seq2feature probe are the outputs from the 30 hour program which guides and mentors students through the open-ended goal of creating an AI safety related project. Many of us are aware we need to grow AI safety as a field in order to give us a chance of keeping up with the advancing model capabilities. The well-intentioned suggestions and advice usually given to budding researchers is: "Work on something where you can have the most impact" "Recreate someone else's work" "Make a new benchmark" "Upskill on general engineering so that you can contribute to someone else's idea" Let's say someone interested in AI safety takes one of these suggestions on board. Then what? Usually their weak and delayed reward signal for their months or years of efforts comes from publishing a paper or landing a job at an AI company. What if AI safety as a field picked measurable goals that required research about an AI model's internal computation? Would this give these researchers a way to focus their time and effort? A rapidly crystallising AI safety risk is that our diffuse efforts across the field will leave us with many immature safety solutions. This exposes us to safety risks as the world's frontier AI developers hone their ever more capable and intelligent models. Competitive AI Safety For any person joining the field of AI safety who is already motivated and has 'good taste' (the definition of this characteristic is always left as an exercise for the reader) loose goals and directions are fine. They'll figure something out. But what impact will this have on the rest of the field? This advice encourages diffuse work with success dependent on each researcher's taste. Will this prevent their work from compounding? AI safety sub goals are often clearly defined but are based around narrow or bespoke scenarios. Usually two proposed solutions to a RFP or research grant can't be easily compared, leading to diffuse work and a lack of coordination between AI safety researchers. However, in competitive model training any two solutions can be compared using a single number letting the contestants' work speak for itself as solutions compound and iterate towards an optima. Competitive model submissions are compared using a single number: nanoGPT speedrun - train an LLM to reach 3.28 FineWeb loss as fast as possible nanoGPT slowrun - lowest FineWeb validation score from 100M tokens and unlimited compute OpenAI Parameter golf - 16MB LLM with the best FineWeb bits per byte score trained in 10 minutes By releasing a baseline and a way to verify each result a contestant can submit a winning score as long as they understand something about model training, failure modes, designing tight feedback loops or model computation better than their opponents. In the OpenAI Parameter Golf contest each new leading solution added an improvement on a previous submission. Someone adds a hashing table and then someone else changes the tables dimensions. Someone runs a hyper parameter sweep to find an optimal setting only to have their score be supplanted by someone else who edits the model's architecture so that it can be compressed more efficiently. The most successful OpenAI Parameter Golf approaches were inspired by bleeding edge model efficiency patterns. This is how creative researchers have fun. The rules for the competitions were set such that solutions could be scaled or refined allowing researchers to compete on the frontier. In my project submission I take lessons from the OpenAI Parameter Golf by maintaining my probe's performance while slashing its size. The shape of these problems mean that iterative solutions are rewarded and once contestants reach a plateau someone will need to come up with a novel approach to unlock the next frontier. Proxy goals are common in AI safety but do not always offer an effective loss function to learn more about a model's risks. One such example is detecting LLM bias using a Red and Blue team approach : a Red Team teaches a model to hold a specific bias, for example, and the Blue Team tries to uncover it. While proxy goals have the best intention of uncovering a model's dangerous capabilities, they are at risk of being a practice in detecting a Red Team's intervention. We need to make it possible for thousands of AI safety researchers to contribute to the field by targeting AI safety ground truths and working on what compounds. A winning solution in Competitive AI Safety on a problem of this shape is at risk of having succeeded not by discovering a truth about the model, but by accurately modelling the Red Team. The selection of loss functions in AI safety that encourage compounding work is perhaps one of the biggest opportunities of Competitive AI Safety. If the Competitive AI Safety contest rewards optimising a single benchmark or creating tooling for a specific model then the work is less likely to be able to compound. Code the perimeter or lose by 100x Kevin Greer delivered this highly insightful talk examining a technology-defining ideological battle that occurred during the development of two OSs. One was called Unix, which is predecessor to the OSs powering the majority of computers globally, and the other one was called Multics. Both OSs had to include a set of operations ( sorting , copying , storage ) for different types of data ( users , devices , processes ). Multics was a collaborative effort between hundreds of developers at MIT, General Electric and AT&T, but they were outclassed by a team of two: the famous programming duo of Dennis Ritchie and Ken Thompson. This duo had previously been a part of the Multics project and so were perfectly placed to know how to maximise their effectiveness by 'coding the perimeter'. Multics' programmers developed each operation for each datatype individually. However, as Greer explains, when Unix added a new operation, they developed it to be compatible with each type of data. For example, Team Multics added the copy operation to the device datatype, and then separately to the file datatype. Team Unix designed interfaces such that once they added the new copy operation the device , usergroup or process datatype would already be able to use it. The mirror image of this also applied to all operations as new datatypes were added. Both would inherit all available abilities without the need for additional work. There are further excellent points made by Greer so I recommend listening to the full talk. To implement 8 operations and 8 data types the Multics approach requires 64 pieces of work. The Unix 'code the perimeter' approach needed 16 pieces of work to implement the same features. When scaled to an entire OS's feature set, even with 100x more developers, Multics couldn't keep pace against two prodigious Unix developers leveraging quadratic utility growth. Maybe the two developers were prodigious because of their working environment or innate talent, or maybe their tremendous output came from making decisions like this one. AI safety faces the same risk that led to the demise of Multics. One researcher develops a detector for a Qwen model and another researcher creates a RL alignment testing environment for a Kimi model and now there are two instances of diffuse work which cannot compound. Competitive AI safety will focus on developing solutions across the field of AI safety to allow researcher's efforts to be measurable and compound. If safety work doesn't leverage the exponentially increasing utility of compounding work it might not fall short by a small margin, but by orders of magnitude. Competitive AI Safety is a forcing function to promote 'coding the perimeter'. Cost, accuracy, portability, compression and speed are factors that can compound. They are reusable across different applications and classes of model. We will need to pick if we are going to continue with the Multics approach or design goals that let us leverage exponentially compounding research and tools. With Unix and Multics they had two growing axes which increased utility quadratically; datatypes and operations . In Competitive AI safety we have many axes such as cost , portability , size , accuracy and memory footprint . Since all axes interact, when there is a 10% reduction on cost or memory footprint by one tool or approach each other tool and approach reaps this benefit also. These efficiencies can stack exponentially like compound interest. My goal of distilling a large SAE into a probe for use on text and across models is something that would greatly increase the probe's potential application. The features of being text-only, low cost and model agnostic expanded the applications of this probe to continuous token monitorability, concept gated routing and probe activated sentry models. By 'coding the perimeter' (maximising portability and cost) this example shows the compounding progress that Competitive AI safety is intended to produce. AI Safety's Loss Function AI model developers were already highly coordinated as they advanced LLMs to where they are today, but coordination wasn't all that was necessary for progress. When the rest of the AI industry needed to make progress, they didn't succeed until they found the right loss function. For LLMs, success came after they started trying to predict the next token in internet text, and later by using humans to train preference reward models. There was no single algorithm that unlocked LLM reasoning and CoT. The reasoning paradigm arrived thanks to appropriate synthetic data and a reward model that could encourage good reasoning. Neo-labs outside of the US had to push the frontiers of pre-training memory management; this has blossomed into a suite of new approaches to make model training more efficient. Their loss function was the delta between their model performance and a frontier model's performance. They had to find improvements in their training pipeline as a way to drive this delta down. It worked and their models caused one of the biggest ever market upsets to AI companies. AI developers are familiar with the trap of Goodhart's law - "When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure". We don't need to find a single benchmark and say we have solved AI safety. This is another lesson the AI research industry has learnt on their quest to make smarter models. The constant addition of AI benchmarks that haven't been optimised for by AI developers has been a reality check on this process of 'benchmaxxing'. "Making AI go better" is not a loss function. We can make AI go better by picking specific measurable goals such as AI safety model size and accuracy on an established safety pipeline. Competitive AI Safety is a platform to direct the creativity and efforts of AI safety researchers to develop stronger and more scalable safety solutions. The replication of an SAE looks related to Goodharting due to their debated position in the field of AI safety. The reality is that they are used extensively in the field and capturing some of their usefulness at a lower cost is an example of 'coding the perimeter' of AI safety. The safety analysis section of the recent Claude Mythos model card at section 4.5 made use of an SAE. This is why I picked them as a candidate to optimise competitively. I didn't have anyone to compete with in this first project. However, I could still battle file sizes and training loss... Section 2: Technical walkthrough of seq2feature - BlueDot AI Safety project submission This section is a technical outline of the research and development process for my BlueDot project submission. Common AI training expressions and terms are not introduced for non technical readers and this is intended to be a more technical view of the work I did. We don't understand the internal computation of LLMs. We need a suite of tools to even attempt to try and make sense of their billions of activations. One of the tools in this suite is the Sparse Autoencoder . An SAE is a model trained to predict the distinct concepts an LLM appears to represent in its activations. We can pass the activations from the specific LLM layer it was trained on (already you can see this is a narrow description) and it will tell us what the model might be thinking about. As we generate the next token in the sentence "The cat sat on the..." we can ask the SAE what concepts appear to be active: "Tokens indicating location or position on a surface, path, or within a system." "Tokens indicating location or position, often with prepositions like 'on'." "This latent detects animals, particularly mammals like bears, wolves, and rabbits." If we could attach an SAE to every model at every layer we could monitor all tokens from every agent and CoT trace and chat model response. Before an LLM can take an action it needs to output tokens to execute code or call tools. An SAE would let us have a classification layer on top of all black box models, lowering the cost of monitorability. However, SAEs are extremely memory intensive to train. Think petabytes of activations. They are trained per model layer and they are not transferable between AI models. An SAE trained on a Qwen doesn't plug into or understand a Kimi model's SAE. Obviously the models share internal representations with each other that can be seen in the text they produce. Ask any model "who is the Sunday red t-shirt american golf guy?" and they will all say Tiger Woods. I wanted to see if the text that the models produced held a signal about the internal concepts that an SAE would detect in the model while the outputted text was produced. I conducted about 300 experiments to complete this investigation. Approach The goal was to use a Gemma 9B SAE as a teacher model and distill its predictions into a tiny probe. The SAE for a single model layer is a few hundred MB and the Gemma model that produces the activations requires gigabytes of VRAM. The pipeline of running a model, hooking into its activations and using the SAE to predict which concepts are active in the model is not a pipeline that will scale as fast as AI model proliferation. My seq2feature 5.3MB text-only probe reproduces 90% of the capability of an SAE on held out text. It scored wins against pre-trained embedding models and bag of words baselines. It also fails legibly when used out of distribution. This probe is small enough to run on a CPU enabling the live monitoring of local coding agent traces and classifying thousands of agent tokens per second on consumer hardware. Try that with an SAE. The training pipeline The pipeline was simple. Run text through the Gemma model and grab some activations from a middle layer. This is the training input to our teacher SAE. We can do a one off pass on a GPU to make a training corpus of output text and SAE labels. We want our probe to learn to predict the labels the SAE would have predicted for a span of text - without seeing the model's activations. One contrast is that the SAE uses the in-flight activations that are on their journey to becoming the next token whereas our probe is making predictions after a token has already been generated. LLMs need to produce a token before they can take any action and so this is what we will monitor. An issue with SAEs is that after concepts have been separated from a model's activations they are labelled based on the types of text that they become active on. Just seeing a unique concept in an SAE doesn't tell us the whole story. Some are straightforward concepts like 'references to the colour blue' but others are more nuanced and tougher to discern. A 'base64 feature' looks very similar to a 'base64 encoded ascii feature' . We feed training data into the model+SAE pipeline and record each segment where a specific SAE feature is active giving us a per feature set of examples. The labelling process is laborious and so LLMs are usually used. When dealing with older SAEs we must be mindful that this automated labelling was probably done with an older LLM. Scoring Based on the fact that an SAE predicts dozens of concepts for every token, I decided to take each concept that fires over a span of tokens and group them together. By matching spans between the SAE and the seq2feature probe I can avoid any tokeniser mismatch which would make per token distillation impossible. During training, I pass the text span as the input with the concepts occurring in the span as the target to my student model which tries to predict which concepts are present as well as their activation magnitude. The SAE used each token's activations at training time, but I wanted to distill its intelligence and remove the cumbersome training time harness at inference time. This is an extremely inexpensive and simple to implement supervision pipeline since we just pass tokens into the SAE and read their labels as the students training data - straightforward distillation. seq2feature uses a novel tokeniser to save disk space as the Gemma tokeniser was not optimised for parameter golf solutions and per span instead of per token grounding would let me map the important parts - concepts. The probe can see all the tokens in a given span and predicts each of the present latents for each token. By inspecting the failure profiles of each model iteration I checked if the probe predicts the strongest firing concepts and if it trips up on OOD concepts. For the next section on architecture selection, I trained different types of probes to predict if a label would fire or not on a token in its own context as compared to the teacher SAE. The training loss was defined by comparing which of the 2048 labelled concepts detected by the student were also detected by the teacher. Corpus The SAE labels had been written by an older LLM. This means that for only $0.80 of Gemini 2.5 flash lite API credits I could enhance the captions to be more useful for a researcher. The captions were not probe targets and so this did not affect training. We don't need to know the old labels since we want to use the more modern model to write an accurate label using the real data. I also did a second pass with the latent to verify it fires on a span inspired by the latent. I created a new dataset of 2048 labels and trained the probe using all of them. For displayed results, I selected 874 captions which had passed a validation (step 5) to aid readability. LATENT #75 — how one concept becomes a label 1. The SAE points to where it fires: "the water was [cold] and [frozen] solid" "keep the samples [chilled] below 4°" "[ice] on the [refriger]ator coils" 2. A cheap model reads those and names it: "Cold, chilled, or frozen states and temperatures" 3. Scoreboard: 874 of 2,045 captions passed this test. The rest still ship, marked "≈" (name unverified). In my initial tests I started with FineWeb as a dataset to train the student. This is not the best dataset to use as it is not representative of the type of content we want to monitor. It included few examples of code and its random structure was unlike a common LLM output which usually has a coherent conversational pattern. The datasets I enhanced my training pipeline with were: domain dataset docs web HuggingFaceFW/fineweb (sample-10BT) 1,200 code bigcode/the-stack-smol 900 reasoning (CoT) open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-114k 900 math open-r1/OpenR1-Math-220k 600 chat Anthropic/hh-rlhf 600 I also collected some OOD data to test the transferability of the probe and these were not used during training. medical — ccdv/pubmed-summarization legal — coastalcph/lex_glue (ledgar) Architecture and code golf Using a sharper lens than just 'how many concepts fire' I wanted to check how many of the top-5 SAE ranked concepts were detected by each architecture. This is a check to see: of the probe's top-5 strongest activations, how many are present in the SAEs firing set. An experimental risk was if few concepts fire on average then a probe that is overly cautious might beat a probe that can usefully detect the labels present in a span. I used the simple loss for the training of the probes (since they just want to learn and we can easily push the capacity of a small model) but when selecting between probes I trusted a top-5 ranked precision more. By checking the shuffled null result to see how bad random labelling was (0.068) we could see that there was a low chance a very bad solution would score well. A model that always selects the top-5 most common latents achieved a score of 0.297/1. This is the confident baseline and it loses to a bag of words approach which scored a surprisingly high 0.84. This is a finding of note as it indicates much of an SAE's computation is recoverable from text. Using top-5 agreement as my loss function I can train probes with architectural refinements iteratively, in keeping with OpenAI's parameter golf challenge, to narrow the gap between random labelling and the SAE ground truth. Each probe is small enough to train in a few minutes on colab. If we embed a span with an embedding model then we expect to recover some of the SAE labels. A label for 'basketball' the sport is likely to be recovered from an embedding of "Michael Jordan is a basketball player". A pre-trained embedding model will store semantics but unfortunately a span such as "harmful content" will return a very similar result to a span of "not harmful content". Hashing was a common theme in Parameter Golf and so I tried adding hashes and an attention head. This already pushed us close to the frontier with a score of 84%, matching a bag of words, and this has helped solve some of the contextual problem. Probe sizes were around 30MB and we haven't even started parameter golfing yet. We don't have a theory of computation for AI models and so we must empirically measure any training approach. My architectural decisions were inspired by related works or my own intuitions but without a measurable target of top-5 agreement, I would never know if I had iterated towards a better model. A model that can be expressive and could learn some semantics while also learning to discriminate patterns is one that will score well. Modern LLMs use a large proportion of their early layer's computation to combine embeddings into n-grams. We want our model to blend these tokens together using our harness. Hashing decouples the size of the model from the vocabulary size and we care about capability per byte, due to our loss function. If we can save a lot of memory and maintain a good level of capability then we will be able to make a more scalable AI safety tool. A bigram hash allows us to store the relationships between bigrams and our hashing encourages the reuse of parameters. It is also highly compressible. Hashed tables and a small transformer brought us 84% precision on the top-5 SAE concepts at a size of 12MB, still matching a bag of words! Hash tables were a key element in the winning OpenAI parameter golf challenge submissions. The seq2feature architecture is near its finalised shape of : We blend unigram, bigram and positional values and pass it into a 1.5m parameter transformer. Up to this point I had not optimised the transformer or optimiser. This is what we need to beat bag of words. The model is so small that AdamW actually outperforms muon. I tried model soup (minor degrading effect), deeper or wider models, smeargates and Swiglu. They all were beaten by a vanilla pytorch transformer! A simple linear -> relu -> linear block and a latent head. Compression session In this investigation we are not only optimising accuracy, but also size. A smaller solution is more scalable and so we need to review the size footprint of each of these approaches to select the right balance between performance and size. approach size top-5 agreement Gemma-2-9B + SAE (teacher) ≈ 18 GB 1.00 (the target) random-5 floor — 0.07 frequency-5 floor (name the 5 commonest) — 0.30 bge zero-shot 33 MB 0.23 bag-of-words (ridge) ≈ 34 MB 0.84 Golf A — stock transformer 92 MB 0.953 Golf B — own tokenizer 59 MB 0.940 Golf C — factorized tables 21 MB 0.935 Golf D — entropy head 21 MB 0.948 Golf E — smeargate (not shipped) 17 MB 0.947 Golf F — soft distill, fp32 21 MB 0.956 Golf F — int8 (seq2feature) 5.3 MB 0.956 Golf F — int4 2.65 MB 0.936 The decisions made during architecture configuration gave me several ways to reduce the size of the model. A bigram table is compressible and I can try code books and quantisations. There were many negative results using codebooks, mixed precision and I didn't do an exhaustive hyper parameter search. This was due to me being more interested with applying proven parameter golf techniques and improving on where on the accuracy gradient seq2feature would land between a full SAE pipeline and a simple embedding model. The int8 variant is lossless at 5.3MB and a smaller 2.6MB int4 probe shows 2 points of precision loss. I think I will accept the browser extension sized probe with a slightly better accuracy. The final seq2feature scores 0.116 higher than a 34MB bag of words while also being one sixth the size. This points to the amount of unoptimised memory usage in the naive bag of words and usefulness of transformer computation in this classification task. Competitive AI safety researchers will be rewarded for leveraging deep learning knowledge. Maximising MFU, avoiding loss spikes or enhancing rollout quality are all useful additions to the AI safety researchers tool kit. Analysis of scoring and failure cases When the seq2feature probe lists the top 5 concepts it thinks fired on a span, it selects concepts that actually fired 19/20 times. The probe can say if any one of the 2048 SAE labels fired on a span with 90% accuracy versus 75% for a bag of words, 55% for a zero shot embedding and ~50% for random guessing. OOD analysis of probe The probe was trained on agent relevant domains such as math, code and chat. There are many domains to which it was not exposed where we can test its OOD performance. Compared to our probe, the SAE teacher was trained on unfathomable amounts of data and so had the opportunity to learn from a diverse set of domains. On the topic of legal and medical domains the probe can say if a label is present in a span 75% of the time. Random labels succeed in this binary classification 50% of the time, or random chance, and the naive embedding scores 55%. Encouragingly when we check the top 5 concepts that seq2feature has detected in a span we can see that they were legitimately present in the SAE firings 94% of the time. This selection of labels also influenced the data that the probe was trained on. While labels such as grammatical syntax can be predicted in a OOD sample, the probe fails in the cases where a concept does not map to one of the probe's 2048 labels. This failure mode bubbles up as far as the SAE as it also can only detect concepts within its dictionary.
