summary: Introduces FineServe, a dataset and characterization of global LLM serving workloads, aimed at improving the efficiency, latency, and throughput of large language model deployments as online services.

title: Hybrid LSTM-Graph Neural Framework for Robust Financial Fraud Detection and Adversarial Resilience
summary: A paper proposing FraudShield AI, a hybrid framework integrating LSTM and Graph Neural Networks to enhance robust financial fraud detection, particularly against complex money laundering patterns.

title: OpenEvoShield: Dual Non-Stationary Continual Defense for Open-World Multi-Agent System Attacks
summary: Introduces OpenEvoShield, a dual non-stationary continual defense mechanism designed to protect LLM-based multi-agent systems from dynamic attacks where adversaries inject malicious instructions.

title: Benchmarking Confidential GPU Inference on NVIDIA H100 under Intel TDX
summary: Benchmarking the performance cost of confidential GPU inference on NVIDIA H100 under Intel TDX for AI inference workloads, specifically for large language model serving with sensitive inputs.

title: FormulaSPIN: Self-Play Fine-Tuning for Natural Language to Spreadsheet Formula Generation
summary: FORMULASPIN is introduced as a self-play fine-tuning framework for generating spreadsheet formulas from natural language, aiming to overcome limitations of static supervised data in existing approaches.

title: Information Discernment in Large Language Models
summary: A study formalizing and investigating information discernment in large language models, examining how they weigh information from external sources and update based on source reliability and truth.

title: NEXUS: Structured Runtime Safety for Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: NEXUS (Neural Execution Utility and Safety) is presented as a structured-plan safety monitor for tool-using LLM agents, applying a formal intervention policy to ensure runtime safety during high-impact actions.

title: Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems
summary: Introduces Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding, a new method designed for multiobjective generative recommender systems to construct item slates that satisfy multiple objectives beyond just relevance.

title: LISA: Linear-Indexed Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Reasoning
summary: Introduces LISA (Linear-Indexed Sparse Attention), a new method designed to enable efficient long-context reasoning in AI models by addressing the O(n^2) computational complexity of standard self-attention for longer sequences.

title: Profile-Graph Memory for LLM Agents: Implicit Cross-Entity Traversal through Narrative Profiles
summary: Introduces Profile-Graph Memory for LLM agents to facilitate implicit cross-entity traversal through narrative profiles, alongside MemHop, a new multi-hop memory benchmark.

title: Lifted Representation Hypothesis in Language Models
summary: Proposes the Lifted Representation Hypothesis to study how large language models store, select, and revise general rule-like structures, and update their internal memory based on observations.

title: GraphContainer: A Unified Platform for Comparing and Debugging Graph RAG Methods
summary: GraphContainer is introduced as a unified platform for comparing and debugging various Graph RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) methods, aiming to address the fragmentation and incompatibility of existing approaches.

title: AdaRoPE: Not All Attention Heads Should Rotate and Scale Equally
summary: AdaRoPE is presented as a novel approach to Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) in Transformers, allowing attention heads to rotate and scale non-uniformly for improved positional information encoding.

title: Statistically Grounded Sparse-Feature Interventions for Activation-Space Control in Large Language Models
summary: Introduces a statistically grounded sparse-feature intervention pipeline for activation-space control in large language models, offering a transparent alternative to fine-tuning for behavioral control.

title: Logic-Guided Data Extraction with Answer Set Programming and Large Language Models
summary: A paper proposing a logic-guided data extraction method that combines Large Language Models with Answer Set Programming to improve reliability for semantic data extraction from unstructured text.

title: Geometry-Guided Constraint Learning for LLM Safety Classification
summary: A method for geometry-guided constraint learning is presented to improve LLM safety classification by optimizing constraint count through sparse autoencoder feature extraction, achieving high accuracy on safety categories.

title: Rethinking Uncertainty Evaluation in Large Language Models
summary: A paper re-evaluating the current methods for assessing uncertainty in large language models, arguing that calibration alone is insufficient and proposing new criteria for interpreting LLM confidence.

title: Spectral-LSH: Sub-Quadratic Prompt Compression via Krylov-Projected Locality-Sensitive Hashing
summary: Introduces Spectral-LSH, a training-free prompt compression method that uses Krylov-Projected Locality-Sensitive Hashing to reduce the quadratic cost of long-prompt inference in language models.

title: Mitigating Scaffolding Collapse in Socratic Tutors via Representation Alignment
summary: Proposes representation alignment to mitigate 'scaffolding collapse' in LLM-based Socratic tutors, preventing them from prematurely revealing solutions under sustained student pressure.

title: CrackedPDFs: A Controlled Benchmark for Hidden Prompt Injection in PDFs
summary: Introduces CrackedPDFs, a controlled benchmark containing 29,322 generated PDFs to evaluate hidden prompt injection vulnerabilities in document-based LLM systems.

title: HyGRL: Adaptive Hybrid Graph Reasoning for Multi-Entity Questions
summary: Presents HyGRL, an adaptive hybrid graph reasoning approach designed to improve retrieval-augmented language models' ability to answer complex multi-entity compositional questions.

title: ITPEval: Benchmarking Formal Translation Across Interactive Theorem Provers
summary: Introduces ITPEval, the first benchmark for formal translation across interactive theorem provers, aiming to improve training data and portability in machine learning for theorem proving.

title: FORCE-Bench: A Benchmark, Dataset, and Evaluation Harness for Agentic AI in Enterprise Finance
summary: Presents FORCE-Bench, a benchmark, dataset, and evaluation harness specifically designed to measure the capabilities of agentic AI systems in operational finance workflows.

title: The Chronos Vulnerability: A Taxonomy of Temporal Persistence and Memory-Based Deception in Agentic AI
summary: Identifies and taxonomizes the 'Chronos Vulnerability,' a form of temporal persistence and memory-based deception that emerges in stateful, autonomous AI agents.

title: Sophisticated Policies from Epistemic Priors
summary: Explores Sophisticated Inference, a variant of active inference, arguing its role in making active inference closed-loop within a planning horizon by allowing future actions to depend on future states.

title: Knowledge-Centric Self-Improvement
summary: Proposes a 'knowledge-centric' view for self-improving AI systems, shifting optimization from agents and workflows to the underlying knowledge to enhance maintainability and transferability.

title: Edge Intelligence in Civil Aviation: Paradigms, Techniques, and Applications
summary: Examines edge intelligence paradigms, techniques, and applications in civil aviation, addressing challenges like high task latency and lack of offline capability for large AI models.

title: Symbol and Footprint Database for Electronic Components by Agentic Recognition and Generation
summary: Develops a system using multimodal LLMs and agentic recognition to automate the creation of symbol and footprint databases for electronic components in PCB design.

title: Silent Failures in Multimodal Agentic Search:A Diagnostic Taxonomy and Cross-Judge Evaluation
summary: Presents a diagnostic taxonomy and evaluation of 'silent failures' in multimodal agentic search systems, which can miss reliability issues in their search trajectory despite accurate final answers.

title: Rewarding Better Thinking for LLM Preference Alignment
summary: Proposes rewarding better thinking as a new approach for LLM preference alignment, moving beyond outcome-level proxy rewards to optimize models toward human preferences.

title: Know Your Agent: Reconnaissance-Driven Pentesting of AI Agents
summary: Introduces a reconnaissance-driven penetration testing methodology for AI agents, formalizing the process to uncover unseen weaknesses and build stronger attacks.

title: DocOps: A Verifiable Benchmark for Autonomous Agents in Complex Document Operations
summary: Introduces DocOps, a deterministically verifiable evaluation framework to benchmark autonomous agents' ability to manipulate complex digital documents.

title: MOF-Sleuth: Tool-Grounded Reward Alignment for Explainable Fine-Grained MOF CIF Auditing
summary: Develops MOF-Sleuth, a tool-grounded reward alignment system for explainable fine-grained auditing of crystallographic information files in metal-organic framework databases using LLMs.

title: SenWorld: A Digital-Twin Simulation for Generating Context-Rich Evaluation Data
summary: Introduces SenWorld, a physically grounded digital-twin simulation designed to generate privacy-safe, context-rich evaluation data for smartphone personal assistants.

title: EvoThink: Evolving Thinking in Large Reasoning Models via Self-Pruning and Aha-Moment Preference Optimization
summary: Presents EvoThink, a method that uses self-pruning and Aha-Moment Preference Optimization to evolve thinking in large reasoning models and mitigate overthinking by distinguishing beneficial from redundant steps.

title: The Giant Hippocampus: From Structural Monoculture to a System of Systems
summary: Compares current AI architectures to biological brains, arguing for a shift from 'structural monoculture' like the Transformer to a 'system of systems' approach inspired by the cortex.

title: Coordinating from Memory: Graph-Structured Experience Reuse for Multi-Agent Adaptation in Dynamic Manufacturing
summary: Presents a method for multi-agent systems to coordinate effectively in dynamic manufacturing environments by using Graph-Structured Experience Reuse for memory and adaptation.

title: CLARK: Closed-loop Learning for Adaptive Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs
summary: This paper introduces CLARK, a closed-loop learning method for adaptive reasoning over knowledge graphs, addressing the challenge of deteriorating model performance with changing data distributions.

title: EvoDRC: A Self-Evolving Agentic Framework for Automated DRC Violation Repair
summary: This paper presents EvoDRC, a self-evolving agentic framework designed to automate the repair of design rule violations (DRC) in physical design, a process that typically requires manual intervention.

title: Reading and Steering Representations of Materials-Science Mechanisms in an Open-Weight Language Model
summary: Researchers investigate how an open-weight language model, google/gemma-4-E4B-it, represents and utilizes materials science mechanisms, showing that this information exists in three separable forms.

title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
summary: This research introduces PRO-LONG, a programmatic memory system designed to enable long-horizon reasoning and sustained perception for large language model (LLM) agents, addressing current performance limitations.

title: TRUST-ESD: A Risk-Calibrated and Governance-Aware AI Framework for Enterprise Strategic Decision Support Under Uncertainty
summary: The TRUST-ESD framework is proposed for enterprise strategic decision support, focusing on AI systems that are risk-calibrated, governance-aware, and uncertainty-aware, beyond just accuracy.

title: CUSUM-Shaped Inference-Time Monitoring and Targeted Re-Decoding for Quantized Small Language Model Reasoning
summary: This work develops MGT-B, a CUSUM-shaped inference-time monitoring and re-decoding technique to prevent quantized small language models from entering repetitive or unproductive reasoning trajectories.

title: PoTRE: Test-Time Reasoning inspired by Cognitive Heterogeneity
summary: PoTRE is a new test-time reasoning method for large language models, inspired by cognitive heterogeneity, aiming to improve their performance on complex reasoning tasks requiring long-horizon planning.

title: Train the Model, Not the Reader: Decodability Supervision for Verifiable Activation Explanations
summary: This paper introduces Decodability Supervision as a method for generating verifiable activation explanations in natural-language autoencoders, aiming to make AI models more interpretable and trustworthy.

title: SoftReason: A Fully Differentiable Neuro-Soft-Symbolic Deductive Reasoning Architecture over High-Dimensional Perceptual Data
summary: SoftReason is presented as a fully differentiable neuro-soft-symbolic deductive reasoning architecture that operates over high-dimensional perceptual data, integrating knowledge graphs for predicate vocabulary.

title: Stateful Guardrails for Multi-Turn LLM Systems: A Conversational Risk Accumulation Framework
summary: This research proposes a Conversational Risk Accumulation (CRA) framework for stateful guardrails in multi-turn LLM systems, addressing safety issues that arise from sequential interactions rather than isolated turns.

title: Economic Evaluations of Language Models
summary: EconEvals is introduced as an open-source evaluation suite designed to measure the economic value and capabilities of language models across various tasks, work activities, and occupations.

title: Challenges of Explainability in Continual Learning for Time Series Forecasting
summary: This work investigates the challenges of explainability in continual learning for deep learning models used in time series forecasting, particularly in real-world environmental monitoring applications.

title: Scale-Aware Learning of Chaotic Dynamics on Unstructured Meshes via Binned Spectral Losses
summary: This paper introduces a method for scale-aware learning of chaotic dynamics on unstructured meshes using binned spectral losses, improving surrogate modeling for high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems.

title: Simulating Eutopia: Revisiting Long-term Fairness with Outcomes, Performativity, and Dynamics
summary: This paper revisits the concept of long-term fairness in AI-driven decision-making, specifically in the context of credit lending, to understand how AI systems can amplify or mitigate social biases.

title: LAARA: Layer-Aware Adaptive Rank Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
summary: LAARA (Layer-Aware Adaptive Rank Allocation) is proposed as a method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning that assigns adaptive ranks to individual transformer layers, improving upon uniform rank allocation.

title: Cross-Subject Semantic Decoding with Shared-Space Alignment for Generalized Neural Representation Learning
summary: Researchers propose a cross-subject semantic decoding framework with shared-space alignment to address the challenge of generalizing neural representation learning across different individuals in invasive recordings.

title: Native Multi-Dimensional Subquadratic Operators via Input Dependent Long Convolutions
summary: This paper explores native multi-dimensional subquadratic operators using input-dependent long convolutions as alternatives to attention mechanisms for processing multi-dimensional data like images and volumes.

title: Bayesian Wind Tunnels for Model Selection
summary: This research introduces model-selection Bayesian wind tunnels as controlled environments to evaluate whether transformers can perform Bayesian model selection and identify correct hypothesis classes from data.

title: CruiseBench: A Real-Flight-Aligned N-CMAPSS Benchmark for Engine RUL Prediction
summary: CruiseBench is introduced as a new benchmark for engine Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, aligned with real-flight data and extending the N-CMAPSS dataset with complete in-flight time series.

title: Air Quality Arena: A Large-Scale Multi-Region Ground Monitoring Dataset and Benchmark for Air Quality Forecasting with Time-Series Foundation Models
summary: Air Quality Arena is presented as a new large-scale, multi-region dataset and benchmark for air quality forecasting using time-series foundation models, addressing the critical public health priority of accurate predictions.

title: STN-TGAT: Top-K Portfolio Construction via Prior-Guided Graph Attention with Learnable Soft-Threshold Sparsification
summary: This paper introduces the Soft-Threshold NMI-prior Transformer Graph Attention Network (STN-TGAT) for stock ranking and portfolio construction. It jointly models temporal dynamics and cross-sectional dependencies in realistic investment settings.

title: Building Fast, Evaluating Slow: Pipeline Choices Dominate Autointerpretability Score Variance
summary: This paper examines how pipeline choices influence autointerpretability score variance when evaluating sparse autoencoder interpretability. It highlights the need for stable properties in evaluation scores for meaningful cross-paper comparisons.

title: The Orthogonalized Read Is a Removable Training Scaffold for Recurrent Memory
summary: This research investigates orthogonalizing the mLSTM memory matrix at read time, finding it improves noisy associative recall during training but is not a fundamental memory improvement. It suggests this technique acts as a temporary training scaffold.

title: Predicting Groundwater Arsenic Concentrations Using Graph Neural Networks
summary: This paper describes using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to predict groundwater arsenic concentrations, aiming to identify high-risk areas and support mitigation efforts. It addresses a significant public health crisis in the United States.

title: From Trajectories to Prefixes: Reusing Teacher Trajectories via Replayed Prefixes and Online Continuation
summary: This research proposes a method to improve the training of small language models for interactive agents by reusing teacher trajectories through replayed prefixes and online continuation. This aims to make distillation more efficient in long-horizon environments.

title: Leveraging Offline Supervision for Efficient and Generalizable Reinforcement Learning in Large-Scale Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This paper explores leveraging offline supervision to achieve more efficient and generalizable reinforcement learning (RL) in large-scale vision-language-action models. It aims to combine the benefits of online and offline RL for improved policy performance.

title: Predictive single cell foundation model for gene regulation and aging with privacy-preserving tabular learning
summary: This research introduces Tabula, a privacy-preserving single-cell foundation model designed for gene regulation and aging analysis. It addresses the unique tabular structure of single-cell data that current models often overlook.

title: When Does Consensus Beat Voting? A Critical Analysis of Statistical Label Fusion in Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This paper provides a critical analysis of statistical label fusion in medical image segmentation, investigating when consensus segmentation methods outperform voting. It derives the mathematical foundations from first principles.

title: Structured Latent Space Modeling over Multi-Scale Temporal Patches for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: This research introduces M2Patch, a CNN-based method for multivariate time series forecasting that uses structured latent space modeling over multi-scale temporal patches. This approach aims to better exploit the organizational geometry of temporal patterns.

title: Reproducing Recurrent Transformers: The CoTFormer
summary: This paper describes and evaluates the CoTFormer architecture, which formalizes Chain-of-Thought as recurrent latent computation. It aims to preserve intermediate states as attendable representations to mimic explicit reasoning traces.

title: NMR Elucidation as an Agentic Search Problem, Not a Modeling Problem
summary: This research demonstrates that an agentic AI system can perform structural elucidation from Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) data, a task typically challenging in chemistry, materials science, and biology. The system achieves a performance level comparable to graduate students.

title: Reward-Aware Population Scaling of Evolutionary Strategies in LLM Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper investigates the reward-aware population scaling of Evolutionary Strategies (ES) for fine-tuning large language models. It explores ES's memory efficiency, parallelism, and compatibility with various black-box or discrete rewards.

title: Adaptive Multi-Expert Graph Transformer for Interpretable EEG-Based Diagnostics
summary: This research presents a Spatial Multi-Expert Graph Transformer designed for interpretable EEG-based diagnostics. The model addresses dynamic changes in neural synchrony by modeling EEG recordings as sequences rather than static features.

title: Marine Engine Fault Dataset: Open-Access Data under Controlled Reference and Fault Scenario Conditions
summary: This work presents the Marine Engine Fault Dataset, an openly available dataset from controlled fault experiments for marine-engine predictive maintenance. It aims to address the scarcity of such datasets with documented operating conditions and subsystem-level interventions.

title: Guardrails as Scapegoats: Auditing Unfaithful Safety Refusals in Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces a black-box auditing framework to assess unfaithful safety refusals in tool-augmented LLM agents. The framework addresses shortcomings in current evaluation methods that overlook silent infrastructure failures and malformed payloads.

title: REGEN: Replay-recycling for Expert-to-Generalist distillation with Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research introduces REGEN, a replay-recycling method for expert-to-generalist distillation using offline reinforcement learning. It aims to improve scaling and efficiency in large language model training for advanced abilities like agentic tool use.

title: Predictive Extrema, Unprofitable Policies: An AI-Assisted Audit of Candle-Based Binance Spot Timing Models
summary: This paper presents an AI-assisted audit of candle-based machine-learning models used for cryptocurrency trading. It evaluates whether these models can generate profitable policies on Binance Spot after accounting for assumed costs.

title: Generating Bearing Vibration Signals at User-Specified Fault Probabilities Using PR-GAN and Counterfactual Methods
summary: This research describes using PR-GAN and counterfactual methods to generate bearing vibration signals at user-specified fault probabilities. This aims to create more 'gray-zone' samples crucial for maintenance decision-making, which are often rare in datasets.

title: MoA-Structured Decode Attention DNF Derivation, KV-Cache Accumulation, GQA/MQA, and OpenACC Kernel
summary: This paper derives four memory-optimal inference artifacts for transformer attention using the Mathematics of Arrays (MoA). The artifacts focus on aspects like KV-Cache accumulation and GQA/MQA to optimize decode attention.

title: Total Variation Distance Estimation in Autoregressive Models
summary: This research investigates the problem of estimating total variation distance in autoregressive models. It aims to quantify distribution differences arising from various LLM deployment and inference optimizations.

title: Do Sheaf Neural Networks Use Holonomy? A Measure--Intervene--Control Study
summary: This paper investigates the internal mechanisms of sheaf neural networks (SNNs) by introducing a basis-independent measurement of trained triangle-loop products to understand if geometric properties drive their predictions.

title: Geospatial Diffusion-based Evolution Synthesis (GeoDES) for Storm-Centered Weather Augmentation
summary: This research introduces Geospatial Diffusion-based Evolution Synthesis (GeoDES), a method designed to improve the prediction of detailed structures in large-scale weather systems like cyclonic storms using machine learning.

title: SynPre-FL: Synthetic data-driven pretraining integrated Federated Learning training framework
summary: This paper introduces SynPre-FL, a federated learning framework that uses synthetic data-driven pretraining to address data sharing limitations and client heterogeneity for privacy-preserving clinical risk prediction.

title: The C-index illusion: discrimination without calibration in published survival models
summary: This research argues that relying solely on the C-index for evaluating survival analysis models leads to misleading comparisons because the metric ignores crucial calibration aspects.

title: Trustworthy Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Federated Learning for Personalised Breast Cancer Prediction
summary: This research investigates the use of trustworthy privacy-preserving multimodal federated learning to develop robust predictive models for personalized breast cancer prediction using sensitive health data.

title: Agent-Centric Animal Pose Forecasting
summary: This research introduces a framework for agent-centric animal pose forecasting using data-driven generative models to understand animal behavior at an algorithmic level in neuroscience and ethology.

title: End-to-End Differential Privacy in Training Deep Neural Network Classifiers
summary: This paper explores methods for achieving end-to-end differential privacy when training deep neural network classifiers to ensure individual data protection with sensitive datasets.

title: The Mechanism Matters: When Knowledge Graphs Help Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research systematically investigates the impact of knowledge graphs on reinforcement learning, providing a comprehensive account of when injecting prior knowledge from KGs helps, hinders, or has a neutral effect.

title: SCPP: A Unified Python Library for Soft Clustering
summary: This paper introduces SCPP (Soft Clustering Python Package), an open-source Python framework that provides a scikit-learn-compatible interface for standardized soft clustering model training, prediction, and evaluation.

title: HypEMBER: Hypernetwork-based Ensemble for Robust Policy Learning of Parametrized Dynamical Systems
summary: This research introduces HypEMBER, a hypernetwork-based ensemble method for robust policy learning in reinforcement learning, addressing the control of parametrized dynamical systems amidst uncertainties.

title: Anatomy of a Sound Neural Reasoner: One-Shot Amortization, First-Pass Poisoning, and Search Inertness in Clue-Rich Completion
summary: This paper analyzes the Lattice Deduction Transformer (LDT) as a neural reasoner, demonstrating its one-shot commitment behavior in clue-rich Sudoku and revealing insights into its internal problem-solving mechanisms.

title: Expert-Guided Forecast Editing for Time-Series Foundation Models
summary: This research proposes expert-guided forecast editing for time-series foundation models, allowing human experts to directly incorporate feedback and refine AI-generated forecasts.

title: Efficient Clustering with Provable Guardrails for LLM Inference at Scale
summary: This research proposes an efficient clustering method with provable guardrails to reduce inference cost and latency, enabling LLM-based applications to scale to millions of users.

title: How Fast Can Reward Models Score? A Systems Study of C++ and PyTorch Inference Runtimes for RLHF
summary: This systems study investigates the inference runtimes of reward models in RLHF pipelines, comparing C++ and PyTorch implementations to identify bottlenecks that slow down policy updates.

title: Koopman Dreamer: Spectrally Constrained Latent Dynamics for Stable World-Model Imagination
summary: This paper proposes Koopman Dreamer, a new Dreamer-style world model featuring spectrally constrained latent dynamics to enable stable world-model imagination for improved sample efficiency in continuous control.

title: Analytic Distribution of Classifier-Free Guidance for Schedule Design
summary: This paper provides an analytic distribution of classifier-free guidance (CFG) for schedule design, analyzing its deterministic guided dynamics in conditional generation for diffusion models.

title: The World Model Remembers, the Actor Forgets: Dream Rehearsal for Continual Model-Based RL
summary: This research introduces "dream rehearsal" to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in model-based reinforcement learning agents, specifically within the DreamerV3 family, when trained on sequential tasks.

title: AlphaRoute: Large Language Models as Semantic Optimizers for Multi-Objective Routing
summary: This paper introduces AlphaRoute, a system that utilizes Large Language Models as semantic optimizers to tackle the NP-hard multi-objective VLSI global routing problem.

title: An Isotropy-Preserving Spectral Cap for Muon: Theory and Three Case Studies
summary: This preliminary report theoretically analyzes the effect of Muon and related matrix-sign optimizers on the internal geometry of weight matrices during large language model pre-training.

title: OPIUM: Mitigating Steering Externalities and Over-Refusal via Dual Objective Latent Optimization
summary: This paper introduces OPIUM, a dual-objective latent optimization method designed to mitigate steering externalities and over-refusal issues when controlling large language models at inference time.

title: Auto-Fill: Learning to Predict Missing Values Accurately with Specialist Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a method using specialist language models to accurately predict missing cell values in tabular data for improved data cleaning. It focuses on the application of AI for a specific data science problem.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Regret for Reinforcement Learning without Horizon Dependence
summary: This research proposes a new algorithm for horizon-free regret minimization in finite-horizon tabular Markov decision processes and provides a theoretical upper bound for its regret.

title: Waymo robotaxis had 68% lower crash rate than human drivers, IIHS study finds - WUSA9
summary: A study by the IIHS found that Waymo robotaxis had a 68% lower crash rate compared to human-driven vehicles, highlighting the safety performance of autonomous mobility.

title: When Reasoning Narrows the Move: Diversity Collapse in LLM Game Play
summary: This research paper explores how supervised fine-tuning can lead to a "diversity collapse" in large language models' game play, narrowing their behavioral options in sequential decision-making.

title: On the Computational Complexity of Structural Generalization
summary: This paper provides a formal mathematical definition for structural generalization, a concept previously measured by benchmarks but not formally described.

title: Scaling Laws for Hypernetwork-Based Knowledge Injection in Large Language Models
summary: This research explores the use of hypernetworks for reliable and scalable injection of factual knowledge into large language models during training.

title: Task Competence Is Not Instruction Following: Evaluating Instruction-Conflicting Behavior in Small Language Models
summary: This research investigates whether small language models follow instructions when they conflict with their usual task behavior, evaluating their instruction-following capabilities.

title: Adaptive Capitulation: A Structural Failure Mode of LLM Responses in Vulnerability Contexts
summary: This paper identifies "Adaptive Capitulation" as a structural failure mode in large language model responses within emotionally sensitive contexts, highlighting ethical challenges in LLM behavior and safety.

title: Reference-Free Evaluation of Reasoning in Open-Ended Question Answering
summary: This research proposes a new reasoning-based, reference-free framework for auditing and evaluating the multi-step reasoning capabilities of large language model outputs in open-ended question answering.

title: Multi-Mask Diffusion Language Models for Few-Step Generation
summary: This paper introduces Multi-Mask Diffusion Language Models, a new approach designed to improve the quality of few-step generation in masked diffusion models.

title: SLPO: Scaling Latent Reasoning via a Surrogate Policy
summary: This paper introduces SLPO (Scaling Latent Reasoning via a Surrogate Policy), a new method to improve the efficiency of reinforcement learning for latent reasoning in Chain-of-Thought reasoners.

title: Lightweight Person-Place Relation Extraction from Historical Newspapers with Dependency Graphs and Proximity Features
summary: This research proposes a lightweight method for extracting person-place relationships from multilingual historical newspapers using dependency graphs and proximity features.

title: Beyond Relevance-Centric Retrieval: Rubric-Oriented Document Set Selection and Ranking
summary: This paper introduces a "Rubric-Oriented Document Set Selection and Ranking" method to improve the quality of retrieved document sets for large language models and AI agents, enhancing their downstream generation.

title: Learning the Arabic Dialect Continuum as a Continuous Space: A Regression Approach to Speaker Origin Prediction
summary: This research presents a regression-based approach using a hierarchical neural architecture to predict Arabic speaker origin by modeling dialectal variation as a continuous geographic space.

title: TriAgent: Divergence-Aware Multi-Agent Committees for Cost-Efficient Financial Sentiment Analysis
summary: This paper introduces "TriAgent," a multi-agent committee system designed for cost-efficient financial sentiment analysis by stratifying agents based on contextual granularity.

title: VizRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Hypergraph Visualization
summary: This research presents "VizRAG," a system that enhances Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by incorporating hypergraph visualization to organize complex n-ary facts.

title: D2VBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models with Value Dilemmas in Daily Scenarios
summary: This paper introduces D2VBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' performance when facing value dilemmas in various daily scenarios.

title: Sentence Splitter: Uncovering Latent Factual Structure for Self-Supervised Learning
summary: This paper introduces "Sentence Splitter," a self-supervised framework built on a T5-based architecture to uncover the latent factual structure within natural language sentences.

title: emb-diversity: A Tool for Embedding-Based Measurement of Data Diversity
summary: This paper introduces "emb-diversity," a new tool designed for embedding-based measurement of data diversity, crucial for developing fair and robust NLP models.

title: Overview of FinMMEval 2026 Task 1: Multilingual Financial Multiple-Choice Question Answering
summary: This paper describes FinMMEval 2026 Task 1, a new benchmark for evaluating multilingual financial multiple-choice question answering systems across English, Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi.

title: Overview of FinMMEval 2026 Task 2: Multilingual Financial Short-Answer Question Answering
summary: This paper describes FinMMEval 2026 Task 2, a new benchmark for evaluating multilingual financial short-answer question answering systems over diverse linguistic evidence.

title: Efficient Chain-of-Modality Reasoning via Progressive Compression for Spoken Language Models
summary: This research proposes a method for efficient chain-of-modality reasoning via progressive compression to improve the mathematical question-answering abilities of spoken language models.

title: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Explainability in Media Bias Detection
summary: This paper presents a multi-dimensional evaluation methodology for assessing explainability in AI systems designed for media bias detection, emphasizing the need for transparent reasoning.

title: When Does Knowledge Distillation Hurt? Reliability-Aware Distillation for Low-Resource Language Summarization
summary: This research investigates the reliability of knowledge distillation for low-resource language summarization, finding that its benefits are modest on the BanSum Bangla benchmark and proposing reliability-aware distillation.

title: TINY_SCHILLER: A Drop-In German Drama Corpus for Small Language Models
summary: This paper introduces TINY_SCHILLER, a new small, single-file German drama corpus designed for prototyping, fine-tuning, and research with small language models.

title: TalentCLEF at CLEF2026: Skill and Job Title Intelligence for Human Capital Management
summary: This paper introduces TalentCLEF, an evaluation challenge for CLEF 2026 focused on developing NLP systems for skill and job title intelligence in Human Capital Management.

title: Language-Specific versus Cross-Lingual Knowledge Graphs for Implicit Aspect Identification in Arabic: A Comparative Study of Reasoning and Adaptation Strategies
summary: This comparative study investigates the effectiveness of language-specific versus cross-lingual knowledge graphs for implicit aspect identification in Arabic aspect-based sentiment analysis.

title: Solar Open 2 Technical Report
summary: This technical report introduces Solar Open 2, a new 250B-A15B Mixture-of-Experts language model with a 1M-token context window designed for long-horizon agentic tasks.

title: The Two-Process Theory of Machine Self-Report
summary: This paper proposes the Two-Process Theory of Machine Self-Report, a theoretical framework for understanding and eliciting reliable self-reports from language models for safety evaluations and public understanding.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Selective Evidence Adoption from Contaminated Retrieval Results
summary: This research explores using reinforcement learning to enable large language models to selectively adopt relevant evidence from contaminated retrieval results, improving accuracy and safety in retrieval-augmented generation.

title: Two-Step Occupation Coding
summary: This paper presents a novel two-step approach for occupation coding, a task that links job titles in free text to occupational taxonomies for labor market research.

title: Understanding the Impact of Linguistic Realization Choices on LLM Stance with Causal Tracing
summary: This research uses causal tracing to understand how linguistic realization choices and constructional variations in prompts systematically impact the stance and decisions of large language models.

title: OpenSkillRisk: Benchmarking Agent Safety When Using Real-World Risky Third-Party Skills
summary: This paper introduces OpenSkillRisk, a new benchmark for evaluating the safety of LLM-based agents when integrating and utilizing real-world, potentially risky, third-party skills.

title: Back to Back with a Copy: A Computational Analysis of AI-Generated Visual Contemporary Art Pastiches
summary: This computational analysis investigates the ability of generative AI models to create contemporary art pastiches and examines the consistency of multidimensional stylistic evaluation across different LLMs.

title: SLAI T-Rex: Full-Parameter Post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 Family on Ascend SuperPOD
summary: This paper details the system-level challenges and methods for full-parameter post-training of trillion-parameter-scale Mixture-of-Experts models from the DeepSeek-V4 family on an Ascend SuperPOD.

title: Gotta Catch them all: the modes of Sycophancy
summary: This research paper analyzes different modes of sycophancy in large language models, challenging the assumption that it is a single behavioral dimension and exploring its implications for alignment and safety.

title: surprisal is Not a Theory
summary: This paper argues that Surprisal Theory is not a computational-level explanation, critiquing its characterization within computational psycholinguistics and the movement towards black box systems.

title: HalluTruthQA: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Hallucination Detection, Localization, and Explanation in Arabic Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces HalluTruthQA, a new fine-grained benchmark for detecting, localizing, and explaining hallucinations in Arabic question answering generated by large language models.

title: On the Systematic Challenges of Culturally Loaded Machine Translation: Dream of the Red Chamber as the Cultural Lens
summary: This research investigates the systematic challenges of culturally loaded machine translation, using 'Dream of the Red Chamber' as a case study to highlight issues beyond surface linguistic forms.

title: Exposure is Optional: Learning Unlike Coordination in Language Models
summary: This paper investigates how language models learn linguistic coordination, challenging traditional views on constituent conjunctions. It explores the nature of language learning within LLMs.

title: The Maskability Index: Predicting Task-Objective Alignment in Pretrained Language Models
summary: This paper introduces the Maskability Index (MI), a new metric designed to predict the alignment between prompting strategies and pretraining objectives in large-scale language models like T5 and BERT.

title: Which Values Do LLMs Confuse? A Schwartz-Based Recognition Study
summary: This study evaluates how Large Language Models identify and confuse human values, specifically using Schwartz's ten basic values as a recognition task.

title: Sound Probabilistic Safety Bounds for Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes a novel framework using Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals to compute rigorous probabilistic safety bounds on the likelihood of a Large Language Model generating harmful output.

title: PyroDash: Cost-Efficient Token-Level Small-Large Language Model Collaborative Inference
summary: This paper introduces PyroDash, a cost-aware framework for token-level collaborative inference between small and large language models, aiming to achieve cost efficiency while maintaining reasoning capabilities.

title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books
summary: This study investigates the impact of generative AI on the book market by using AI detection to analyze over 14,000 self-published genre-fiction works.

title: Notes to Self: Can LLMs Benefit from Experiential Abstractions?
summary: This research investigates whether Large Language Models can benefit from "experiential abstractions" to improve problem-solving, similar to how humans distill and apply past experiences.

title: LKValues: Aligning Large Language Models with Sri Lankan Societal Values
summary: This research addresses the cultural bias in Large Language Model value alignment by focusing on aligning LLMs with Sri Lankan societal values, aiming to prevent mishandling of local cultural dynamics.

title: Auditing Retrieval-Augmented LLM Hypotheses for Longitudinal Cell Painting Morphology
summary: This paper discusses auditing Retrieval-Augmented LLM hypotheses for interpreting longitudinal Cell Painting morphology data, aiming to translate cellular state signatures into interpretable biology.

title: JailMeter: An Evidence-Based Evaluation Framework for Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes JailMeter, an evidence-based evaluation framework designed to consistently and reliably measure the success rates of jailbreak attacks against large language models.

title: BaseRT: Advancing Best-in-Class LLM Inference with Apple M5 Neural Accelerators
summary: This paper introduces BaseRT, a native Metal inference runtime for Large Language Models on Apple Silicon, designed to exploit the dedicated Neural Accelerators within Apple's M5 generation GPU architecture.

title: Twin Agent: Context Residual Compression for Privilege Separated Agents
summary: This paper introduces "Twin Agent," a system that uses context residual compression for privilege-separated agents to mitigate security risks like prompt injection attacks in Large Language Model agents.

title: Detect Early, Escalate Rarely: Anytime Detection of AI-Generated Video from the Compressed Bitstream
summary: This research proposes a method for "anytime detection" of AI-generated video directly from the compressed bitstream, recasting the task as streaming perception.

title: Crowd4D: Scene-Aware Monocular 4D Crowd Reconstruction
summary: This paper introduces Crowd4D, a method for scene-aware monocular 4D crowd reconstruction from video, addressing challenges like depth ambiguity and complex scene geometry.

title: D3VL: Understanding Driving Scenes from 3D Time Series Data and Video with Language Models
summary: This paper presents D3VL, a method that leverages Multimodal Large Language Models to understand driving scenes by integrating 3D time series data and video for autonomous driving applications.

title: ChronoStitch: Training-Free Composition of Visual KV Memories for Long-Horizon Temporal Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces ChronoStitch, a training-free method for composing visual key-value memories from video chunks, enabling long-horizon temporal reasoning in vision-language models for tasks like long-video question answering.

title: EGRNet: A Lightweight Semantic Segmentation Network with Edge-Gated Refinement and Adversarial Sensing
summary: This paper introduces EGRNet, a lightweight semantic segmentation network featuring edge-gated refinement and adversarial sensing, designed for efficient and robust scene understanding in applications like autonomous vehicles.

title: Pathologist Attention-Aligned Report Generation for Prostate Histopathology
summary: This research explores pathologist attention-aligned report generation for prostate histopathology, aiming to improve medical imaging tasks like cancer diagnosis by incorporating human visual attention.

title: Domain Shift in Echocardiography: Interpretable Quantification and Prediction of Cross-Dataset Left Ventricular Segmentation
summary: This study investigates domain shift in echocardiography for left ventricular segmentation, focusing on interpretable quantification and prediction of cross-dataset generalization as a barrier to clinical deployment.

title: A Unified Variational Framework for Deep Weakly Supervised Image Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes a unified variational framework for deep weakly supervised image segmentation, utilizing a simplex-constrained Potts model with a smooth perimeter regularizer as a training loss.

title: PhenSPINE: A Standardized Benchmark for Spine Pathology Diagnosis
summary: This study introduces PhenSPINE, a new standardized benchmark dataset of 16,813 MRI images from 250 patients for spine pathology diagnosis. It aims to improve the evaluation of automated diagnostic systems for spinal conditions.

title: SafeGen: Goal-Conditioned Video Diffusion of Safety-Critical Scenarios for VLM-Based Autonomous Driving
summary: SafeGen introduces a goal-conditioned video diffusion method to generate safety-critical scenarios for evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) used in autonomous driving systems. This addresses the need for rigorous testing under rare but dangerous situations, especially involving vulnerable road users.

title: Point-Selection Fine-Tuning Framework for Robust Point Cloud Classification
summary: This paper proposes a point-selection fine-tuning framework designed to improve the robustness of point cloud classification models. It addresses performance degradation caused by noisy and corrupted data, particularly in 3D pre-trained models.

title: Efficient Tracking and Understanding Object Transformations
summary: This research focuses on developing more efficient methods for tracking objects that undergo state transformations in real-world dynamics. It aims to reduce the high computational cost of existing tracking methods like TubeletGraph.

title: Extending a Large View Synthesis Model for Multi-view Panoptic Segmentation
summary: This study explores extending large view synthesis models to perform multi-view panoptic segmentation by leveraging their learned spatial correspondence, which generalizes beyond just appearance. This enables new applications for existing view synthesis architectures.

title: DRGBT-1K: A Large-scale High-quality Benchmark for Dynamic RGBT Tracking
summary: This paper introduces DRGBT-1K, a large-scale and high-quality benchmark dataset specifically designed for evaluating dynamic RGBT tracking models. It aims to assess model performance in scenarios where sensing modalities and observation platforms change over time.

title: Look Before You Edit: Attention-Guided Camera Placement and Multi-View Alignment for 3D Gaussian Splatting Editing
summary: This research presents LB-Edit, a framework for attention-guided camera placement and multi-view alignment to enhance text-driven 3D scene editing using 3D Gaussian Splatting. It aims to overcome limitations of fixed camera views in editing complex 3D environments.

title: WASABI: Whole-graph Assignment-based Stabilizer for lAne topology By Inter-frame tracking
summary: WASABI introduces a whole-graph assignment-based stabilizer that uses inter-frame tracking to improve the understanding of lane topology for autonomous driving systems. This enables better navigation through intersections and reasoning about complex traffic scenarios.

title: Trace: A Taxonomy-Guided Environment for Multidomain Visual Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces Trace, a taxonomy-guided environment designed to provide broad, verifiable, and reproducible training data for multidomain visual reasoning in vision-language models. It aims to extend reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to the vision domain.

title: Lean-SAM2: Target-Anchored Memory and Encoder Acceleration for SAM2
summary: Lean-SAM2 introduces optimizations including target-anchored memory and encoder acceleration to improve the efficiency and deployment of the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2). This addresses issues like heavy memory cross-attention overhead in the original model.

title: Memory-Augmented Multimodal Large Language Models for Small Object Understanding in Streaming Aerial Videos
summary: This research explores the use of memory-augmented multimodal large language models to improve small object understanding in streaming aerial videos from UAVs. The memory mechanism is critical for handling sequential frame data in real-time perception.

title: Robust Activation Map Rectification for Weakly Supervised Volumetric Segmentation: Temporal Coherence as a Free Lunch
summary: This paper proposes a method for robust activation map rectification in weakly supervised volumetric segmentation, leveraging temporal coherence to address noisy and failure-prone class activation maps. It aims to improve localization accuracy without additional computational cost.

title: Current Injection Spiking Neural Network for Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
summary: This research introduces a current injection spiking neural network (SNN) for infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF). It aims to integrate complementary information from both modalities into a single image, offering an alternative to traditional artificial neural network methods.

title: MTVDiff: Multimodal Conditional Latent Diffusion for Enhanced Thermal-to-Visible Face Translation
summary: MTVDiff proposes a novel multimodal conditional latent diffusion framework designed to enhance thermal-to-visible face translation. It integrates depth and textual information to address challenges like geometric discontinuities and identity degradation.

title: LAVIFT: Latent-Action-Guided Vision Fine-Tuning for Surgical Interaction Recognition
summary: This research introduces LAVIFT, a latent-action-guided vision fine-tuning method aimed at improving surgical interaction recognition for context-aware and autonomous robotic surgery. It utilizes pretrained vision-language models to understand instrument-tissue interactions.

title: OSVE: One Step Video Editing with One Step Diffusion Models
summary: OSVE is presented as the first framework to successfully adapt one-step text-to-image diffusion models for high-quality video editing. It addresses the computational slowness of multi-step sampling in text-guided video editing.

title: StrokeSeg2: Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Clinical Research Workflows
summary: StrokeSeg2 is introduced as a lightweight, modular framework designed to facilitate the deployment of stroke lesion segmentation models in clinical research workflows. It addresses the challenges of software dependencies and computational requirements found in existing deep learning frameworks.

title: MV-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Coordinated Multi-View Interface Construction
summary: MV-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) specifically for their ability to generate code for coordinated multi-view interface construction. It addresses the limitations of existing evaluations focused solely on single-chart generation.

title: LoRFT: Benchmarking Long-Range Vehicle Trajectory Reconstruction from Fixed Highway Cameras
summary: LoRFT introduces a benchmark for evaluating long-range vehicle trajectory reconstruction from fixed highway cameras. This aims to improve traffic safety analysis and autonomous driving evaluation by providing spatio-temporal evidence.

title: WearWow: Native 2K Multi-Garment Virtual Try-On via Adaptive Token Packing and Preference Alignment
summary: WearWow presents a new framework for native 2K multi-garment virtual try-on, utilizing adaptive token packing and preference alignment. It addresses memory and detail preservation challenges in synthesizing high-resolution digital fashion via diffusion models.

title: G-MAD: A Game-Based Data Generation Framework for Multi-View RGB-T Aerial Object Detection
summary: This work introduces G-MAD, an open-source framework using Arma3 to generate synchronized multi-view RGB-T data for aerial object detection, addressing limitations in real-world aerial dataset construction.

title: SIINR: Structurally Informed Implicit Neural Representations for super-resolution with uncertainty quantification of clinical quality diffusion MRI datasets
summary: This paper introduces SIINR, a method using structurally informed implicit neural representations for super-resolution and uncertainty quantification of clinical diffusion MRI datasets, aiming to improve brain microstructure analysis.

title: ETPDesigner: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Interactive Multimodal Electronic Theater Program
summary: ETPDesigner proposes a multi-agent orchestration framework for interactively generating multimodal electronic theater programs, addressing challenges of existing text-to-image systems with complex visual assets.

title: OffNadirLoc: Benchmark and Framework for Challenging UAV-to-Satellite Geo-Localization under Large Off-Nadir Views
summary: OffNadirLoc introduces a benchmark and framework for UAV-to-satellite geo-localization under challenging large off-nadir views, where extreme perspective distortions and appearance gaps occur.

title: Forecasting the Number of Harvest-ready Fruits of Sweet Peppers Using Multimodal Time-Series Data
summary: This paper introduces a novel, annotated image time-series dataset to forecast the number of harvest-ready sweet peppers using multimodal data, addressing a critical need for precision agriculture.

title: STEREOFLOW: Progressive Stereo Matching with StereoDiT and Transition Flow Matching
summary: STEREOFLOW proposes a progressive stereo matching method using StereoDiT and Transition Flow Matching, addressing limitations of deterministic regression in 3D reconstruction by modeling multimodal distributions.

title: Toward Seasonal Guidelines for Robust Deep-Learning Sentinel-2 Building Detection in Different Area Types
summary: This research focuses on developing seasonal guidelines for robust deep-learning-based Sentinel-2 building detection across various area types, addressing challenges with native 10m resolution imagery.

title: A Systematic Benchmark of Intensity Normalisation Methods for 3D Knee MRI Segmentation and Cross-Domain Generalisability
summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark evaluating intensity normalisation methods for 3D knee MRI segmentation, focusing on their impact on cross-domain generalisability for clinical deployment.

title: Importance-Aware OBS Pruning for Diffusion Models
summary: This work proposes importance-aware OBS pruning, a training-free framework for diffusion models that prioritizes preserving parameters critical to semantically salient image regions using spatial importance maps.

title: GaussianSeed: Hierarchical Gaussian Seeding for High-Resolution 3D Occupancy Prediction
summary: GaussianSeed introduces a progressive multi-level hierarchical Gaussian seeding method for high-resolution 3D occupancy prediction, addressing computational challenges in autonomous driving and robotic navigation.

title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
summary: This paper describes the development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful AI tool designed to diagnose cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images.

title: ENTRAP-VL: A Taxonomic Probe for Dual Contextual Entrainment in Vision-Language Models
summary: ENTRAP-VL introduces a taxonomic probe to investigate dual contextual entrainment in vision-language models, analyzing how auxiliary context influences model output, building on prior work in unimodal language models.

title: RIM: A Retrieval-In-Matching Framework for Cross-Domain Global Visual Localization of UAVs
summary: RIM proposes a Retrieval-In-Matching framework for cross-domain global visual localization of UAVs using remote-sensing reference maps, addressing challenges caused by appearance and viewpoint shifts.

title: HeadCast: Casting Attention Heads for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
summary: HeadCast introduces a method for casting attention heads to enable efficient autoregressive video generation, specifically addressing the growing KV cache cost in long and streaming video synthesis.

title: Real-Time EEG Cap Electrode Detection for Guided Point-of-Care Placement
summary: This paper presents a two-stage vision system that uses a YOLO detector to localize EEG cap electrodes in real-time and validates their anatomical placement for guided point-of-care.

title: SHFormer: Dynamic Spectral Filtering Convolutional Neural Network and High-pass Kernel Generation Transformer for Adaptive MRI Reconstruction
summary: SHFormer introduces a dynamic spectral filtering convolutional neural network and a high-pass kernel generation transformer for adaptive MRI reconstruction, leveraging attention mechanisms for improved feature representations.

title: StreamHOI: Interaction-aware Temporal Memory Adaptation for Streaming HOI Video Generation
summary: StreamHOI presents a low-latency streaming framework for long-duration human-object interaction (HOI) video generation, utilizing interaction-aware temporal memory adaptation to overcome limitations of offline short-video methods.

title: PerceptDrive: Perception Prior World-Action Modeling with Adaptive Expert Routing for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: PerceptDrive introduces a new world-action modeling approach with adaptive expert routing for end-to-end autonomous driving, aiming to integrate frozen perception foundation models effectively into planning.

title: RS-RIE-Bench: Benchmarking Reasoning-Guided Remote Sensing Image Editing
summary: RS-RIE-Bench introduces a new benchmark for reasoning-guided remote sensing image editing, which aims to modify images based on natural language instructions while preserving geographic and sensor characteristics.

title: Not All Patches are Equal: Sampling Matters for Visible-Infrared Pre-Training
summary: This paper explores the importance of sampling in visible-infrared pre-training for robust multi-sensor perception, arguing against uniform patch-wise contrastive learning due to imaging-physics differences.

title: Vera: Identity-Faithful Human Subject-to-Video Generation
summary: Vera is a method for subject-to-video generation that aims to preserve identity-critical human details, addressing issues of generic subject consistency in generated videos.

title: ModPack: An Extensible Teleoperation Interface for Bimanual Mobile Manipulation
summary: ModPack is a modular and extensible teleoperation interface designed to support diverse robot embodiments and task requirements for bimanual mobile manipulation.

title: Milo, a Fully Autonomous Indoor/Outdoor Robotic Guide Dog
summary: Milo is a fully autonomous robotic guide dog designed to assist blind and low-vision individuals with indoor and outdoor navigation, providing an alternative to traditional guide dogs.

title: LENS: LLM-guided Environment Simplification for Planning and Control in Clutter
summary: LENS (LLM-guided Environment Simplification) is a method that uses large language models to simplify cluttered environments, improving planning and control for robotic manipulation tasks.

title: NavVerse: Benchmarking Indoor-to-Outdoor Embodied Navigation in Continuous Robot Simulation
summary: NavVerse is a new benchmark designed to evaluate indoor-to-outdoor embodied navigation for robots in continuous simulation, addressing the gap in existing benchmarks.

title: Defer to Plan: Adaptive Multi-Agent Fusion for End-to-End V2X Driving
summary: Defer to Plan proposes an adaptive multi-agent fusion framework for end-to-end Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X)-aided autonomous driving, aiming to improve driving performance.

title: V2F: Vision-Informed Grasp Force Prediction for Damage-Aware Robotic Handling of Date Fruits
summary: V2F is a vision-informed grasp force prediction framework designed for robotic handling of date fruits, aiming to prevent damage by considering high detachment forces and low bruise thresholds.

title: Clinical Pathways as Safety Specifications for Physical AI in Hospital Wards
summary: This paper explores the reinterpretation of Clinical Pathways as explicit runtime safety specifications for physical AI systems, including assistive robots, operating in sensitive hospital ward environments.

title: SOPD-SocialNav: Selective On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Social Navigation
summary: SOPD-SocialNav is a method that uses selective on-policy distillation for vision-language social navigation, aiming to deploy effective social navigation capabilities on resource-constrained robotic platforms.

title: KineBench: Benchmarking Embodied World Models via IDM-Free Kinematic Grounding
summary: KineBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the physical consistency of embodied world models using IDM-free kinematic grounding, providing a more faithful assessment than existing methods.

title: EA-Nav: Learning Safe Visual Navigation Policies with Embodiment Awareness

title: ClickGuard: Detecting and Spoiling Clickbait News with Informativeness Measures and Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces ClickGuard, an AI-driven browser extension that uses a hybrid machine learning architecture, combining transformer-based embeddings and linguistic features, to detect and counteract clickbait news. title: Stochastic Sampling is Epistemically Shallow: The Dimensionality Gap Between Temperature Variation and Model Diversity in LLMs
summary: This research paper investigates the phenomenon of stochastic sampling in large language models (LLMs), questioning whether variations in model responses genuinely reflect uncertainty or are merely superficial. It explores the relationship between temperature variation and model diversity.

title: JAXBench: Benchmarking Autonomous TPU Kernel Optimization
summary: This paper introduces JAXBench, a new TPU-native benchmark suite designed for evaluating autonomous AI-generated kernel optimization on Google Cloud TPUs. It aims to drive progress in this area by providing a rigorous, shared target for performance measurement, similar to existing GPU benchmarks.

title: DC-Leap: Training-Free Acceleration of dLLMs via Draft-Guided Contiguous Leaping Decoding
summary: This paper introduces DC-Leap, a novel training-free decoding strategy that significantly accelerates Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) by using a draft-guided contiguous leaping approach. This method aims to improve efficiency by addressing overly conservative confidence thresholds in current parallel decoding strategies.

title: InferenceBench: A Benchmark for Open-Ended LLM Inference Optimization by AI Agents
summary: This paper presents InferenceBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of AI agents in optimizing open-ended large language model (LLM) inference. It aims to assess agent capabilities beyond prescribed workflows and narrow action spaces in research and development tasks.

title: DecodeShare: Tracing the Shared Subspace of LLM Decode-Time Decisions
summary: This research introduces DecodeShare, a protocol designed to identify a consistent low-dimensional subspace within large language model (LLM) decode-time decisions during KV-cached inference. The goal is to understand the task-general structure used during output generation.

title: PlanE: Meta Planning of Data, Tuning, and Inference for Extractive-based LLMs
summary: This paper introduces PlanE, a meta-planning framework that optimizes data, tuning, and inference processes for extractive-based large language models (LLMs). It aims to reduce annotation costs and improve task-specific capabilities by providing better optimization methods for tailoring LLMs.

title: Benchmarking the Personalization Capabilities of Large Language Models
summary: This research focuses on benchmarking the personalization capabilities of large language models (LLMs), evaluating their ability to tailor messages to specific receivers. It contrasts LLM-based personalization with traditional two-party psychological and marketing models.

title: Robust Critics: Defending LLMs Against Multi-Turn Attacks
summary: This paper explores the challenge of defending large language models (LLMs) against multi-turn attacks, focusing on the ambiguity of harmful requests and the need for robust safety mechanisms. It discusses the dilemma between harming legitimate users and being easily exploited.

title: Incomplete Prompt Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
summary: This work formalizes and investigates "incomplete prompt jailbreaks" (IPJ) in large language models (LLMs), a vulnerability where sentence completion can bypass existing safeguards against harmful requests. It demonstrates how open-weight models remain susceptible to such exploitations.

title: VeriSimpl: Robust Optimization Modeling from Natural Language using Simplification-based Verification
summary: This paper introduces VeriSimpl, a method for robust optimization modeling from natural language inputs using large language models (LLMs) through simplification-based verification. It aims to improve the accessibility and usability of optimization modeling by translating textual descriptions into executable solver formulations.

title: SonicSampler: Unified Tile-Aware Kernels for LLM Sampling and Speculative Verification
summary: This paper introduces SonicSampler, a new approach using unified tile-aware kernels to optimize large language model (LLM) sampling and speculative verification during inference. It aims to accelerate the complex logit processing and token selection pipeline, which existing implementations often handle inefficiently.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Multi-Sensor Physical Hazard Assessment
summary: This empirical benchmark evaluates the ability of five large language models (LLMs) to assess multi-sensor physical hazard data across 60 scenarios in categories such as joint assessment, response proportionality, and pattern disambiguation. The study involved 1,800 API calls to measure their performance.

title: Semi-Supervised Text-Attributed Graph Distillation
summary: This paper presents a semi-supervised text-attributed graph distillation method aimed at addressing scalability bottlenecks in representation learning for Text-Attributed Graphs (TAGs), particularly when integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs). The technique helps manage complex graph topology and rich textual semantics.

title: Beyond Liars' Bench: The Impact of Lie Typology, Depth, and Sparsity on Deception Detection in LLMs
summary: This research extends beyond "Liars' Bench" by investigating how different lie typologies, depths, and sparsities impact the effectiveness of deception detection probes in large language models (LLMs). It highlights the challenges of out-of-domain performance for such detection methods.

title: Enabling Scalable Topology Inference in Distribution Systems via Constrained Multi-Source Inference
summary: This paper proposes a method for enabling scalable topology inference in electrical distribution systems through constrained multi-source inference. The goal is to improve accuracy for critical functions like outage localization and voltage analytics, addressing challenges with imperfect utility data.

title: Routing Without Training: Controllable-Ratio LLM Offloading via Reliability Gating
summary: This work introduces a training-free method for controllable-ratio large language model (LLM) offloading between local and cloud resources, utilizing reliability gating. This approach allows for efficient deployment under resource constraints without relying on specific training or fine-tuning for routing.

title: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
summary: This paper introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark designed to evaluate personalized web agents, particularly their ability to infer missing context from user browsing histories when instructions are underspecified. It assesses how well large language model-powered agents can autonomously execute complex tasks based on individual user data.

title: Tractable Hierarchical Control of Autoregressive Language Models
summary: This research proposes a method for tractable hierarchical control of autoregressive large language models (LLMs) to constrain their generation. The aim is to ensure LLMs produce syntactically valid outputs, particularly for tasks such as program synthesis.

title: The Devil is in the Spectrum: Mitigating Representation Collapse in LLMs via Topologically Regularized Side-Path
summary: This paper presents a topologically regularized side-path method to mitigate representation collapse in Large Language Models (LLMs), a bottleneck that degrades long-context performance.

title: Expectation Alignment of Language Models for Real-World User Expectations
summary: This work explores how to align language models with real-world user expectations, highlighting the limitations of current evaluation approaches that fail to capture user diversity.

title: OPTScientist: Multi-Agent Discovery of Typed Optimizer Programs for Transformer Pretraining
summary: OPTScientist is a multi-agent system designed for the automated discovery of typed optimizer programs specifically for transformer pretraining in deep learning.

title: Directional Hallucinations: Ideological Drift in News-Grounded LLM Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces a reproducible measurement framework to analyze and quantify 'directional hallucinations' or ideological drift in news-grounded LLM question answering, particularly in politically sensitive contexts.

title: Autonomous Topology Mutation: Safe Runtime Restructuring for Multi-Agent LLM Systems with Capability, State, and Shadow Invariants
summary: This research introduces autonomous topology mutation for multi-agent LLM systems, allowing them to safely restructure their team at runtime when individual agents become overloaded.

title: EvoSQL: Memory-Augmented Critic-Generator Co-Evolution for Text-to-SQL
summary: EvoSQL is a memory-augmented critic-generator co-evolution framework that improves Text-to-SQL capabilities for complex database queries through multi-step decomposition and execution-based diagnosis.

title: CRAWO: Custom Resources for Adaptive Workload Orchestration
summary: CRAWO (Custom Resources for Adaptive Workload Orchestration) is a framework for managing and deploying AI pipelines at the network edge to enable real-time applications in smart cities.

title: Attention-based Experience Replay Framework for Continual Learning of Agnostic Time Series Forecasting Models

title: Isolating LLM Alignment from Regex: Zero Coverage and Metric-Dependent Divergence Under Adversarial Mutation
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of LLM alignment methods by examining the robustness of regex filters and model-side alignment against adversarial inputs designed to bypass them.

title: Workload-Aware Caching for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: This work proposes workload-aware caching mechanisms for multi-agent systems to efficiently store and reuse intermediate results, optimizing performance across complex task executions.

title: AISE-Bench: A Full-Cycle Curated Benchmark for Information Seeking on Academic Knowledge Graphs
summary: AISE-Bench is a new full-cycle benchmark specifically designed for evaluating tool-using autonomous agents on information-seeking tasks within academic knowledge graphs.

title: ExecuGraph: A Multi-Agent, Execution-Grounded Framework for Reliable Backend Code Synthesis with Large Language Models
summary: ExecuGraph is a multi-agent, execution-grounded framework designed to improve the reliability and correctness of backend code synthesis generated by large language models.

title: FlowEdit: Information-Theoretic Control of LLM Reasoning Flows for Ill-posed Problems Involving Conflicts
summary: FlowEdit presents an information-theoretic control method to guide LLM reasoning flows, enabling them to better handle ill-posed problems involving conflicting or inconsistent conditions.

title: MKEvolve: A Modular Multi-Agent Framework for Kernel Code Generation
summary: MKEvolve is a modular multi-agent framework that iteratively co-evolves a modular decomposition for generating correct and performant kernel code for hardware accelerators.

title: LeanFlow: A Case Study in Workflow-Driven Lean Autoformalization
summary: LeanFlow is an LLM agent system specialized for workflow-driven autoformalization, specifically translating mathematical papers into buildable Lean projects.

title: Optimizing Hypergraph-Based RAG: Toward Better Fact Extraction and Chunk Retrieval
summary: This paper focuses on optimizing Hypergraph-Based RAG by improving fact extraction and chunk retrieval processes to enhance deeper reasoning and accuracy in knowledge graphs.

title: MiniCache: Reusable Program Caching with Small Model Interfaces for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: MiniCache is a reusable program caching framework that enhances the efficiency of LLM inference for program-aided reasoning and agentic decision making by transforming Program-of-Thought (PoT) programs.

title: Telco-GAIA: Bilingual Benchmark for Agents in Telecom Domain
summary: Telco-GAIA is introduced as a bilingual, multi-modal benchmark for evaluating tool-using agents within the telecommunications domain, featuring human-verified question-answering tasks.

title: SiGMA: Sign-Guided Merging and Adaptation for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
summary: This research proposes SiGMA, a sign-guided merging and adaptation method for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT), addressing catastrophic forgetting in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).

title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback
summary: This paper investigates methods for reliability-aware LLM alignment, specifically addressing the challenges posed by inconsistent and subjective human feedback in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF).

title: CANN Bench: Benchmarking Agent Generated Kernels against Real NPU and Algorithmic Limits
summary: AI agents are now capable of writing, compiling, and iteratively optimizing low-level operator kernels on different hardware platforms. Existing benchmarks, however, focus almost exclusively on CUDA and Triton, leaving hardware ecosystems with less-exposed programming models without a common evaluation baseline. We present CANN Bench, an open benchmark for AI-generated operator code on Huawei's Ascend NPU. The current release covers 53 operators and 1060 test cases organized into four difficulty tiers -- from simple elementwise primitives to MoE dispatch and FlashAttention kernels -- spanning FP16, BF16, FP32, and INT8 precision formats. Evaluation adopts a \textbf{three-dimensional weighted composite score} that treats compilation, functional correctness, and performance as independent axes, providing a principled reward signal for kernel-generation agents. Performance is graded against an out-of-the-box PyTorch-on-Ascend baseline and an analytical per-case Hardware-Anchored Performance (HAP) limit on real NPU hardware, ensuring scores reflect genuine optimization headroom rather than measurement artifacts. The evaluation harness is designed to resist reward hacking from the ground up. CANN Bench is versioned within the official CANN repository and is designed for long-term community co-construction, providing the Ascend ecosystem with a quantitative, reproducible, and sustainably maintained yardstick for AI operator-authoring capability.

title: Representation Robustness Under Executable Reasoning Constraints in Large Language Models for Mathematical Problem Solving
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated on mathematical problem solving, yet prior work often treats representationally equivalent formulations as interchangeable and conflates reasoning errors with interface failures. This paper investigates representation robustness in LLM-based mathematical problem solving by systematically varying surface representations of the same underlying problems, including story problems, word-equations, symbolic equations, and isomorphic paraphrases. Using a curated dataset of mathematically equivalent problems, we evaluate five contemporary LLMs under a direct answer generation condition. We find substantial representational sensitivity: models frequently change correctness across equivalent formulations, with nontrivial flip rates across story, symbolic, and word-equation variants. We also observe systematic regressions under isomorphic reformulations, showing that even subtle paraphrase-level changes can degrade performance despite preserved mathematical structure. We then evaluate a code-augmented condition in which models externalize reasoning as executable Python code that is run locally for validation. This interface reveals strong latent reasoning capability in some models that perform poorly under direct prompting, but it does not uniformly improve robustness. Instead, failures shift across interaction layers, from opaque reasoning errors to protocol violations and execution failures.
