Even when executable reasoning succeeds, representation sensitivity often persists. Overall, our results show that reasoning scaffolds do not eliminate representational brittleness, but expose new tradeoffs among correctness, reliability, latency, and cost. We argue that representation should be treated as a first-class interface design variable in LLM evaluation and deployment, especially for AI-assisted problem-solving systems.

title: Attention Degradation, Function Token Anchoring, and the Limits of Attention-Based Intervention in Large Language Models
summary: Mean cross-positional attention degradation is widely reported in transformer interpretability, yet whether it causally limits contextual retrieval remains untested. We present six coordinated experiments across GPT-2, LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B, OPT-1.3B, and distilgpt2. We first characterise short-term (5-100 token) attention degradation, finding a universal exponential-then-plateau pattern whose rate is inversely correlated with depth, with distinct layer-wise entropy signatures per architecture. Function token anchoring proves architecture-dependent: OPT-1.3B (absolute positional encoding) shows distance-dependent preposition specificity, GPT-2 shows uniform non-specific dependence, and LLaMA (RoPE) shows reversal at long distances. Strategic comma insertion at clause boundaries causally reduces prediction degradation in the 40-80 token range, with the benefit tied to syntactic boundary alignment rather than token density. We then test the mechanism causally: Relay-Aware Attention (RAA), which biases attention logits toward function token positions, verifiably increases attention mass by 16-24% yet yields null effects on GPT-2 and LLaMA-1B, preliminary harm on LLaMA-3B, and a mixed effect on OPT-1.3B that nets to approximately zero. Multi-fact retrieval probes further show that degradation rate does not predict retrieval accuracy across models. We conclude that mean attention degradation is largely descriptive rather than prescriptive: function tokens contribute through what their hidden states compute, not through the attention they receive -- with implications for interpretability methodology and attention-score-based inference optimisations such as KV-cache eviction.

title: Autonomous disproofs of the sum-product conjecture over $\mathbb R$ with GPT-5.5 Pro
summary: OpenAI's recent disproof of the Erd\H{o}s unit distance conjecture marked a milestone for AI in mathematics. It also inspired another breakthrough: a human disproof of the Erd\H{o}s--Szemer\'edi sum-product conjecture over $\mathbb R$. In this paper, we present a simple agent built on GPT-5.5 Pro. Using a problem-agnostic, three-stage prompting pipeline -- proof-plan proposal, proof construction, and review -- the agent autonomously generated correct proofs that the sum-product conjecture is false over $\mathbb R$ in 7 of 8 independent trials; in the remaining trial, it identified an unresolved gap in its argument. The seven proofs are diverse: some are close to existing unit-based constructions, while others avoid units by using $L^p$-type regions of algebraic integers. The system used an average of 132.4k reasoning tokens per trial. We release the code, intermediate outputs, and generated proofs, providing a reproducible, data-contamination-free case study in autonomous proof generation.

title: ConfidenceBench: Evaluating Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in settings where fluent but incorrect answers can be costly. In these settings, accuracy alone is insufficient: models must also know when they are likely to be wrong. We present ConfidenceBench, a calibration benchmark that evaluates verbalized confidence estimates in 15 frontier LLMs using the Brier score, a proper scoring rule that incentivises truthful probability reporting. Confidence is elicited via prompting, requiring no access to model logits and making the framework applicable to both closed-source and open-source systems. The benchmark comprises 200 private multiple-choice questions across four categories: spatial reasoning, high-precision mathematics, word lookup, and unknowable questions. Across three independent runs, Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview achieve the lowest Brier scores, both reported as 0.103. Both substantially outperform the calibrated-random baseline of 0.1875, while Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite scores 0.367, indicating severe miscalibration. Accuracy and calibration diverge substantially across model families: the most accurate model is not the best-calibrated, and several models perform worse than the calibrated-random Brier baseline despite reasonable accuracy. These results show that verbalized confidence calibration is a distinct and practically important axis of LLM reliability, complementary to standard accuracy-based evaluation.

title: Evaluating and Guarding Citation Faithfulness in Agentic Scientific Synthesis
summary: Agentic LLM systems such as OpenScholar and PaperQA2 read the scientific literature and return cited answers, and both they and their benchmarks already check whether those citations hold, with a fixed attribution model or human graders. Neither audits the reliability of that check itself. We show it is not reliable, and that this matters. On identical agent outputs the measured unsupported-citation rate ranges from about 3% to about 18% depending only on the verifier's strictness, and although verifiers agree on which citations are supported, they disagree on which to flag (negative-specific agreement 0.27 to 0.30), so no single flag set is trustworthy and cross-paper comparison is invalid without a named verifier and protocol. We present a gold-anchored evaluation protocol and a deployable guard that make this behavior measurable and bounded. The protocol validates the verifier, measures re-attribution, and calibrates a guarantee against human gold rather than another model's verdict; the verifier is a swappable instrument chosen on cost (recall 0.94 on the supported class, held out), and re-attribution is a commodity step where a deterministic BM25 matches the best open generator. The guard adds a split-conformal layer placing a distribution-free, finite-sample bound on truly unsupported citations that slip past a chosen flagging rule, a guarantee on catch rate rather than conclusion correctness. The bound holds on held-out gold, and we identify and quantify the condition governing its transfer to deployment, calibration-negative difficulty, with a concrete recalibration recipe, left untested by prior conformal-factuality work. Validated across four open 27-35B models and three agentic pipelines on public benchmarks (SciFact, QASA, PubMedQA), with confidence intervals on every headline number, the protocol and guard ship as an open single-GPU kit.

title: PromptPack: Scaling LLM Annotation Agents for Online Recommendation
summary: Online recommendation platforms increasingly use Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract structured features from ad creatives. While deploying a single-call LLM annotation agent yields significant Click-Through Rate (CTR) improvements in our live production environment, per-creative prompting is prohibitively expensive to scale. The redundant system instructions sent in every request account for 94% of billed input tokens. To break this cost bottleneck, we introduce PromptPack, a scalable, high-throughput LLM annotation agent. PromptPack achieves this scale via in-context batching, combining a shared system prompt, a strict XML structural envelope, and an output correction layer to ensure deterministic, pipeline-ready feature extraction across multiple creatives simultaneously. We evaluate PromptPack via an offline retrieval benchmark using a downstream logistic-regression ranker. To deeply profile the agent's behavior, we measure AUC and introduce Volume-Weighted Absolute Lift (VWAL), a novel metric capturing the signal quality of the generated features. Compared to our live, unbatched production baseline, PromptPack at batch size 20 cuts our LLM costs by 89% and accelerates throughput by 2.5x while fully preserving AUC.

title: DynamicMCPBench: A Trace-Grounded, Effect-Scored Benchmark for LLM Agents over Live MCP Servers
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed over Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, yet the benchmarks used to evaluate them score the final answer or a fixed "ground-truth" list of tools, both of which are fragile once the underlying data is live and stateful. We present DynamicMCPBench, a reusable framework rather than a fixed dataset. A practitioner can run it on their own MCP servers to test models on their own tasks, or let it collect servers automatically to measure a model's general ability to solve agentic tasks. Given the servers and any set of models, it generates realistic goals, pursues each one live to record a successful trajectory, distills that trajectory into path-agnostic effect checkpoints, and scores an agent on whether it reproduces those effects, never on the final answer. To show what the framework reveals, we run it at scale: 24 models over 121 servers and 750 tasks spread evenly over 15 task categories (50 each), where each category targets a distinct tool-use challenge of the generated questions. Each task is scored by pass^3: it counts as solved only if all three independent attempts succeed. Even the strongest agents solve only about half of the tasks, 31% of tasks are solved by no model at all, and accuracy collapses as the required tool chain grows longer (from 39% on the shortest chains to 13% on the longest). A human validation study confirms the automatic scoring is reliable (chance-corrected agreement of 0.76). DynamicMCPBench thus turns benchmark construction into something practitioners can rerun on their own servers and models, while exposing a consistent inability of current agents to handle long, multi-step agentic tasks.

title: AppWorld-UL: Benchmarking Diverse Agent-User Interactions for Tool-Use
summary: Tool-use agents that address day-to-day digital tasks such as ordering groceries must not only operate applications, but also interact with the user, e.g., to ask clarification questions, prompt for confirmation, and inform the user when the instruction is infeasible. However, current benchmarks for evaluating agent-user interactions do not capture the diversity of such interactions. Further, they operate in small environments with few, often non-state-changing, APIs. To address this gap, we introduce AppWorld-UL, a ``user-in-the-loop'' benchmark of 516 challenging tasks requiring diverse agent-user interactions. Building upon the AppWorld framework with 9 popular simulated apps like Amazon and Spotify, we systematically modify original tasks to introduce ambiguities and constraints that necessitate various types of agent-user interaction. User behavior is simulated by an LLM prompted to respond with carefully designed knowledge boundaries, offering more reliable simulation than the unconstrained or overly rigid alternatives used in prior work. Our evaluation reveals that a state-of-the-art LLM, Claude Opus 4.7, achieves only 48.6% success on AppWorld-UL, and only 35.7% on the harder, compositional subset. On the stricter, scenario-level metric, compositional task performance drops to only 21.3%. Our analysis reveals that correct user-interaction is crucial for success. This demonstrates the benchmark's difficulty and its potential to advance research on user-in-the-loop tool-use agents.

title: StrideDiffusion: Accelerating Diffusion Models for Time-series Generation
summary: Diffusion models have become competitive generators for time series, but their practical use is limited by the large number of sequential denoising steps required at inference time. Existing fast samplers typically use fixed or generic timestep schedules, overlooking a distinctive property of time-series diffusion: different spectral bands evolve at different rates during the reverse process. We introduce StrideDiffusion, a training-free spectral-aware sampler that adaptively selects the denoising stride from band-level activity. At each step, StrideDiffusion monitors relative band energy, log-power drift, and phase velocity to identify whether high- frequency dynamics remain active or whether the trajectory is dominated by stable low-frequency structure. It then takes fine steps when rapidly varying bands are active and larger jumps once only coarse components remain. A bandwise stability analysis shows that inactive frequency bands change only linearly with the jump size under deterministic affine reverse updates, providing a local justification for spectral activity as a step-size indicator. Across six unconditional time-series generation benchmarks, StrideDiffusion uses only 14-66 function evaluations instead of 500/1000 denoising steps, achieving up to 18.9x wall-clock speedup while preserving or improving generation quality. On conditional imputation and forecasting, it further delivers 5-14x average acceleration with comparable predictive accuracy. These results show that spectral evolution provides a practical and principled signal for fast time-series diffusion sampling. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/stridediff-ts.

title: CMI-Mem: Toward Generalizable Long-Term Memory Management via CMI-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
summary: Memory Manager models are pivotal in agent systems. Existing methods rely predominantly on LLM-judged synthetic question-answer (QA) pairs, making memory valuation dependent on sampled queries and the downstream reader. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{CMI-Mem}, a reinforcement learning(RL)-based lightweight memory manager model with a hybrid reward that combines downstream QA correctness and intrinsic Conditional Mutual Information (CMI). CMI evaluates the information contributed by new conversational inputs relative to the current memory state without conditioning on a sampled QA query, thereby complementing rather than replacing QA grounding. Our codes are available at: https://github.com/Wyb0627/CMIMem , and the CMI-Mem-4B model checkpoint is available at: https://www.modelscope.cn/models/wyb0627/CMIMem-4B

title: AI-Driven Multi-Hop Relay Selection for Smart Urban NR-V2X Networks via Learning-to-Optimize Graph Neural Networks
summary: Reliable and low-latency NR-V2X communications are essential for smart mobility in dense urban environments. However, limited Road-Side Unit (RSU) density, frequent non-line-of-sight conditions, and highly dynamic vehicular topologies often prevent many Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) from maintaining stable single-hop connectivity. Although multi-hop relay-assisted communication can extend infrastructure coverage, selecting relay links in real time under practical flow, capacity, and connectivity constraints remains challenging. Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) yields optimal multi-hop relay decisions, but its computational complexity scales sharply with network density, limiting real-time applicability. To address this, we propose a Learning-to-Optimise (L2O) framework based on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for real-time NR-V2X relay selection. Vehicular communication states are modeled as attributed graphs, where CAVs and RSUs are nodes and candidate radio links are enriched with propagation-aware features. An offline MILP oracle provides optimal supervision, while an edge-aware Graph Isomorphism Network (GINE) approximates oracle decisions with near-constant inference latency. Experiments on large-scale urban datasets generated by an integrated SUMO--GEMV2 simulation pipeline show that the proposed approach achieves connectivity comparable to that of the MILP oracle while reducing execution time by orders of magnitude. The framework enables cost-effective enhancement of urban V2X connectivity by leveraging existing vehicular assets and supporting scalable, real-time NR-V2X operation in smart city environments.

title: KeySI: An Interaction Framework for Tuning Text Embeddings Based on Human Feedback
summary: In large-scale text analysis tasks, pre-trained language models are often used to embed text corpora for downstream analysis. However, such models may struggle to capture domain-specific semantics and adapting them typically requires large amounts of labeled data and technical expertise to implement training pipelines. Recent approaches have demonstrated how visual interactions in document projections can capture human feedback as training signals for model tuning. However, these methods operate on document-level feedback, which requires users to open and assess individual documents in order to provide effective feedback. In this paper, we propose KeySI, an interaction framework that enables feature-level feedback through keyword-based concept specification. Users specify feedback by organizing extracted keywords into groups representing concepts, which KeySI translates into document-level supervision for subsequent tuning. By operating on keywords as the primary interaction medium, KeySI reduces the need for manual document inspection and labeling and lowers the barrier to adapting embedding models. We present a prototype implementation that, given a corpus, curates representative keywords, visualizes keywords and document embeddings via dimensionality reduction, allows interactive specification of keyword groups, and supports iterative refinement through system feedback. We evaluate KeySI through a user study, usage scenarios, and quantitative experiments demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing user intent and improving embedding alignment.

title: WaveformQA: Benchmarking LLM Temporal Reasoning on Digital Waveforms
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation and reasoning, yet their ability to perform temporal reasoning over digital waveform data remains largely unexplored. Although reasoning over digital waveforms is a critical bottleneck in design verification, existing benchmarks primarily evaluate hardware description language (HDL) code generation and use waveforms only as supplementary context. This paper presents WaveformQA, an open-source question-answering benchmark for evaluating LLM temporal reasoning over digital waveforms. The benchmark comprises 360 questions with programmatically generated ground truths across eight categories of varying difficulty, including questions targeting multi-signal correlation and event ordering. Waveforms are generated from open-source design implementations, ensuring reproducibility and grounding the benchmark in real hardware behavior. Evaluation of frontier LLMs reveals that while models achieve reasonable accuracy on simple queries, performance degrades due to context window limitations and reasoning difficulties on complex temporal and multi-step questions. In addition, we show that an event-time JSON representation of waveforms improves LLM reasoning accuracy versus the standardized value change dump (VCD) format. The open-source framework supports extending to new question categories and importing new waveform sources, enabling researchers to rapidly prototype temporal reasoning experiments.

title: NVIDIA-labs OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents
summary: Traditional agent development is split across prompt templates, tool schemas, callback code, and workflow graphs. We present NVIDIA Object-Oriented Agents (NOOA), a model-agnostic Python framework for building reliable AI agents. NOOA takes a simpler approach: an agent is a Python object. Its methods are the actions the model can take, fields are its state, docstrings are its prompts, and its type annotations are contracts. A method whose code body consists of "..." is completed at runtime by an LLM-driven agent loop, while methods with normal bodies remain standard deterministic Python. This gives developers and agents the same interface, so agent behavior can be tested, traced, refactored, and improved just like other software. This paper makes three contributions. (1) We present the agent-as-a-Python-object programming model and the design principles behind it. Where Python has existing abstractions, we adopt them directly. Agent-specific capabilities--context, events, state rendering, long-term memory, and validated LLM loops--are exposed through simple Pythonic APIs, so both developers and agents share one familiar programming model. (2) We identify six model-facing ideas that NOOA is, to our knowledge, the first to combine on a single surface: typed input/output, pass-by-reference over live objects, code as action, programmable loop engineering, explicit object state, and model-callable harness APIs for context and events. We find the community already converging on several of these ideas--often as experimental or partial features--and present the comparison to encourage further adoption. (3) We demonstrate that current models use this interface effectively, both in targeted capability tests and on agentic and reasoning benchmarks such as SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 and ARC-AGI-3.

title: ArbiGraph: Arbitrarily Scalable Verifiable Task Graphs for Evaluating Context Management
summary: We introduce ARBIGRAPH, a benchmark generator for evaluating whether tool-assisted language agents can retain, update, compose, and discard task-relevant context across extended reasoning workflows. ARBIGRAPH represents each task as a natural-language problem with an executable Python solver, and composes tasks through typed intermediate states, instantiated here as scalar and list values. This design enables controllable task graphs whose length, dependency structure, distractor count, and value type can be varied while preserving exact automatic verification. We instantiate ARBIGRAPH with math, GSM-style word-problems, and Python-tracing task categories, and evaluate a Qwen3.5-27B tool-assisted agent across four topologies. The results show high accuracy on isolated tasks but substantial degradation on more complex dependent tasks: accuracy drops by up to 33.3% on branching chains of dependent math tasks. This shows that ARBIGRAPH exposes failures that are not visible from single-task evaluation alone. Our code, generated datasets, and evaluation results are available at https://github.com/pavelgolikov/ArbiGraph.git

title: DataPrep-Bench: Benchmarking LLMs as Training Data Preparators
summary: The quality of training data fundamentally determines the capabilities of large language models (LLMs), yet no unified benchmark exists to measure how well LLMs, agents, and data-centric workflows actually prepare training data end to end. We view LLM-driven data preparation as comprising two complementary capabilities: data construction, which transforms raw sources into supervised training data, and data quality evaluation, which predicts the training value of candidate datasets before downstream training; throughout, "quality" refers to downstream training utility rather than surface-level textual properties. We introduce DataPrep-Bench, the first unified benchmark that jointly evaluates both capabilities under a shared downstream-grounded protocol over six domains and multiple base models. For data construction, methods consume identical raw sources and are scored by fine-tuning a base model on their outputs jointly with Dolly-15k; alongside this track we release Data-Construction-Skill, a skill-guided agent that lifts the Dolly-only baseline by nearly 20 points absolute on Llama-3.1-8B Finance and is competitive with the strongest agent- and DataFlow-based methods in knowledge-extraction-dense domains. For data quality evaluation, scoring functions are scored by Pearson correlation with downstream performance on a shared candidate pool; we release the Distributional Alignment Score (DAS), a distribution-based evaluator that uses MMD between a candidate dataset and a domain proxy. DAS attains the strongest cross-model correlation in four of six domains and is the only metric clearing r > 0.70 simultaneously in Math, Science, and Medical, outperforming existing quality-, diversity-, and heuristic-based evaluators. DataPrep-Bench provides a unified, downstream-grounded framework for measuring progress on both capabilities as co-equal targets of LLM-driven data preparation.

title: PhantomFill: When the Form Demands an Answer, Language Models Invent One
summary: Language models in production do not write prose. They fill forms: JSON fields, function arguments, extraction templates. We show that the form itself causes hallucination. We ask thirteen models the same question about the same input and change only the answer format. The inputs are built so the question cannot be answered: a viral post showing 12,400 likes but no visible replies, a support ticket whose call was never transcribed. In free text, GPT-5.5 answers honestly. It says there is no reply data, 98% of the time. Given a required JSON field for sentiment, the same model invents an answer 40 times out of 40. It fabricates the mood of crowds it never saw and quotes customers it never heard. The pattern holds with force. Required fields drive fabrication to 100% in ten of thirteen models. An explicit "insufficient evidence" option rescues only the frontier: all nine open-weight models ignore it. A direct instruction, do not infer sentiment, is overridden by the schema in four of six models. Resistance does not come with scale: within a single model family, the smallest model refuses, the mid-sized model fabricates, the largest refuses again. Honesty under format pressure is a training outcome that no one is measuring. The fabrication hides exactly where hedging is impossible: in required enums and minimum-count arrays, fields where no disclaimer fits. We release PhantomFill, a benchmark with deterministic scoring and two reportable numbers: the Coerced Fabrication Rate and the Escape Utilization Rate. The fix we test is one line of schema. The failure we measure is everywhere.

title: The Active Ingredient in Muon's Grokking
summary: The Muon optimizer reaches the grokking threshold on modular arithmetic faster than AdamW. Prior work attributes this to "spectral-norm constraints plus orthogonalized momentum" but does not isolate which mechanism matters. To better understand Moun's behavior, we run multi-seed and multi-learning-rate sweeps to decompose and stress-test the effect. First, an ablation shows the speedup comes from orthogonalization (the Newton-Schulz iteration): orthogonalize-only matches full Muon, whereas spectral-only is no faster than AdamW and is unreliable, and this verdict holds across learning rates. Second, a mechanistic analysis finds that orthogonalizing optimizers reach generalization at roughly 3x lower spectral norm and, controlling for how much the embedding actually moves, settle into a lower-norm solution rather than simply perturbing the embedding less. Third, reducing the Newton-Schulz iteration count from five to one accelerates reaching the threshold but makes the grokked solution fragile, prone to transient collapse, with fragility that grows with learning rate; a single iteration is fast and stable only at small learning rate, while the canonical five iterations are the learning-rate-robust choice. We also show spectral scaling can be dropped at no measured cost. A methodological thread runs throughout: under a stability-aware metric, "faster" claims about grokking optimizers can invert, so we report both first-crossing and sustained-grok times. To support reproducibility, we release our full training and analysis code at https://github.com/louiswang524/muon-grokking-frontier

title: Scaling Closed-Loop Feature Channel Configuration with LLMs
summary: Promising initial results in closed-loop large-language-model-based channel-configuration search demonstrated that neural-network widths can be optimized directly through executable code generation and accuracy feedback. However, those results were obtained from a relatively sparse set of valid evaluations, leaving open whether the observed optimization behavior transfers to a denser sampling regime and whether additional architectural regularities emerge when more generated networks are evaluated. To test this, the same search setting is scaled to 250 candidate networks per fine-tuning cycle. The analysis covers 2000 generated candidates from 8 complete cycles, yielding 462 verified CIFAR-100 evaluations after task and metadata filtering. Per-cycle mean accuracy exhibits a positive linear trend with slope 9.87e-4 (p=0.043), while the high-performing frontier improves more strongly: the best observed accuracy increases from 0.3144 to 0.3676, and both the top-5 and top-10 cycle-level means exhibit positive trends. The scaled run also reveals improved parameter efficiency. The best model reaches 0.3676 with 11.8M parameters, compared with an early high-performing model at 0.3144 with 166.5M parameters. Beyond accuracy, the larger sample exposes architectural regularities that were difficult to assess from sparse observations. Non-power-of-two channel widths occur in 41.8% of verified candidates, and the strongest models share structured channel-allocation patterns characterized by moderate early widths and expanded middle or later blocks. These findings indicate that the channel-search signal observed in the initial study transfers

title: Multimodal CoLRAG-TF: Triple-Filtered Retrieval for Complex PDFs
summary: This item introduces Multimodal CoLRAG-TF, a four-axis fusion architecture for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over complex and heterogeneous PDF collections. It aims to improve RAG performance by addressing challenges in multimodal content and multi-hop reasoning.

title: Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts
summary: This paper explores adaptive depth in Looped Transformers, analyzing learned halting gates and trajectory readouts. It investigates how these mechanisms influence inference-time stopping rules and training-time loss weighting for recurrent blocks.

title: Generative Bayesian Filtering for State Estimation
summary: This research introduces Generative Bayesian Filtering, a method for inferring the latent state of dynamic systems from observations. It aims to address limitations of classical filtering approaches that often rely on simpler observation models.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Trust Estimation for Multi-LLM Systems via Structured Expert Judgement
summary: This paper proposes a method for Uncertainty-Aware Trust Estimation in Multi-LLM systems using structured expert judgment. It aims to improve the reliability of LLM ensembles by accounting for varying trust levels and uncertainty quality among different models.

title: Position: Stop Reactively Patching Your Model Every Time and Start Proactive Test-Driven AI Development
summary: This position paper advocates for proactive test-driven AI development as an alternative to reactive model patching. It proposes improving the generalization and maintenance of AI systems in diverse use-cases by building robust development pipelines.

title: A Graph Neural Network approach to zero-shot Digital Twins
summary: This research introduces a novel framework for Zero-Shot Digital Twins using a Graph Neural Network approach. It aims to overcome the rigidity of traditional predictive digital twins by allowing adaptation to changing physical domains and boundary conditions without extensive retraining.

title: ReliableTableQA:How Much Supervision Does Reliability Annotation Need?
summary: This paper introduces ReliableTableQA, a framework for training an LLM to annotate the statistical reliability of tabular question-answering results. The goal is to determine if computed answers are statistically meaningful, which is crucial for enterprise analytics.

title: Codec-Gauge: Learning Compression-Friendly Gauges for Transformer KV Caches
summary: This research introduces Codec-Gauge, a post-training method for learning compression-friendly gauges for Transformer KV caches. It aims to improve long-context Transformer inference by optimizing KV-cache compression and quantization.

title: Leveraging Biokinetic Knowledge Priors for Data-Scarce Bioprocess Modeling
summary: This paper explores leveraging biokinetic knowledge priors to address data scarcity in bioprocess modeling, particularly for biomanufacturing. It aims to accelerate the application of deep learning in this domain where experimental data is limited.

title: From Atoms to Entropy: Optimal Noise Allocation for Diffusion Training in the Convex Regime
summary: This research develops a general statistical framework for studying optimal noise allocation in diffusion training. It aims to move beyond heuristic noise schedules by determining the asymptotically optimal noise levels for training diffusion models.

title: Improving Access to Essential Medicines via Decision-Aware Machine Learning
summary: This research explores improving access to essential medicines in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) through decision-aware machine learning. It aims to optimize the efficient and equitable allocation of scarce resources in healthcare systems despite data limitations.

title: When RLVR Shrinks the Reasoning Boundary: Diagnosing Pass@k Inversion
summary: This paper diagnoses "pass@k inversion," a phenomenon where Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves one-sample accuracy but degrades model performance under repeated sampling. It aims to understand why the trained policy solves fewer distinct problems than its base model at large k.

title: Conflict Resolution under Degraded Surveillance in Air Corridors Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: This study develops a Deep Q-Network-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework for decentralized conflict resolution in air corridors. It aims to enable safe Advanced Air Mobility operations by allowing aircraft to maintain separation even with degraded surveillance information.

title: SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales
summary: This research adapts and enhances preconditioned gradient methods to overcome the challenges of large-scale LLM pretraining. It aims to leverage higher-order optimizers like Muon and SOAP for faster convergence while addressing their computational cost and numerical stability issues.

title: SevDiff: Severity-Conditioned Diffusion for Long-Tail Conflict Trajectory Generation
summary: This paper introduces SevDiff, a Severity-Conditioned Diffusion model for generating long-tail conflict trajectories for ADAS evaluation. It aims to address the data imbalance in ADAS datasets by creating synthetic vehicle-to-vehicle conflict events.

title: Beyond SBDD: Geometric Deep Learning in Polypharmacology and Multi-target Drug Design
summary: This research explores the application of Geometric Deep Learning to polypharmacology and multi-target drug design, moving beyond traditional structure-based drug design. It aims to address the challenges of multifactorial diseases like cancer and neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Thermodynamic Weight Decay: Exploring Grokking Acceleration via Attention Specific Heat
summary: This research explores "Grokking" acceleration using "Thermodynamic Weight Decay," analyzing it through the lens of Attention Specific Heat. It aims to understand and potentially mitigate the delayed generalization observed in neural networks, particularly Transformers.

title: Double-Scoring: Reliable Extraction of Strong Lottery Tickets
summary: This paper introduces "Double-Scoring," a method for reliably extracting strong lottery tickets from large neural networks. It aims to find sparse subnetworks within overparameterized models that are already accurate before extensive training.

title: Monkey King Bang: A Unified Scientific Multimodal Foundation Model
summary: This paper introduces "Monkey King Bang," a unified scientific multimodal foundation model designed for multi-domain reasoning in scientific discovery. It aims to bridge the gap between specialized AI systems and general scientific data unification.

title: StabilityBench: Benchmarking Instability in LLMs
summary: This paper introduces "StabilityBench," a new benchmark designed to measure and evaluate instability in Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI Assistants. It aims to better understand the real-world behavior of LLMs in high-stakes settings.

title: Joint Utilization of Geospatial and census proxies for Autoencoder-Assisted Downscaling (JUGAAD) of socioeconomic indicators in India
summary: This research uses autoencoder-assisted downscaling to combine geospatial and census data for monitoring socioeconomic indicators like poverty and food security in India. It aims to address scale mismatches between different data sources for better insights.

title: Chronofy: A Temporal-Logical Decay Architecture for Information Validity in Time-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Chronofy introduces a temporal-logical decay architecture for time-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It aims to improve information validity by considering the temporal relevance of retrieved facts, reducing temporal hallucinations in LLM outputs.

title: CT-Merging: Consensus Directions and Task-Level Scaling for LoRA Adapter Merging
summary: CT-Merging proposes a method for combining independently trained LoRA adapters into a single multi-task adapter. This technique aims to improve the efficiency of deploying specialized models by reducing storage and simplifying task selection.

title: AI-Driven Surrogate Models for Predicting Electrode-Scale Discharge Behavior in Lithium-Ion Batteries
summary: This research introduces an AI-driven surrogate model, based on a Swin3D Transformer, to predict the electrode-scale discharge behavior of lithium-ion batteries. The goal is to reduce the computational cost associated with traditional physics-based simulations.

title: Bayesian uncertainty estimation improves clinical decision making in medical AI agents
summary: This study demonstrates that Bayesian uncertainty estimation, using Monte Carlo dropout, can improve clinical decision-making for medical AI agents. It enhances the reliability of machine learning models for medical image analysis by providing confidence measures.

title: Detecting Neural Network Failures through Spectral Analysis of Internal Activations
summary: This research proposes detecting neural network failures by analyzing "Spectral Drift," a phenomenon of characteristic spectral instability in internal activations during misclassifications. It offers a new method for understanding and diagnosing neural network issues.

title: When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers
summary: This research investigates when a weight-tied looped transformer can implement an algorithm, focusing on convergence selection. It provides findings from controlled populations on group word problems to understand its computational capabilities.

title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
summary: This research investigates the causal necessity and stability of single-token Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) features for interpreting and steering large language models. It examines how these features' roles vary across different SAE families and layer depths.

title: Scaling Interpretable Transformers with Parity Bottleneck Layers
summary: This research proposes scaling interpretable Transformers using Parity Bottleneck Layers to address the phenomenon of superposition in language models. It aims to build models that are interpretable by construction, rather than relying on post-hoc methods like sparse autoencoders.

title: SalesLoop: Reinforcement Learning from Performance Feedback for Sales Lead Ranking
summary: SalesLoop introduces a reinforcement learning approach that uses performance feedback for sales lead ranking in CRM systems. It aims to close the gap between offline model accuracy and real-world production performance.

title: Adaptive Multi-Horizon Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research proposes adaptive multi-horizon reinforcement learning to improve decision-making in complex environments. It aims to dynamically balance short-term and long-term consequences, moving beyond fixed discount factors in RL.

title: Explanation-Based Runtime Verification for Trustworthy ML-driven Optical Networks
summary: This research introduces explanation-based runtime verification to enhance the trustworthiness of machine learning-driven optical networks. It aims to ensure reliable performance and resource allocation in automated network management.

title: CEDAR: Causal Edge Discovery for Autoregressive Processes
summary: CEDAR (Causal Edge Discovery for Autoregressive Processes) is a constraint-based method proposed for identifying lagged causal relationships in sparse autoregressive time series. It screens candidate cross-variable lags using distance correlation.

title: Perspective Latents as an Architectural Condition for Causal Emergence in Active Inference Agents
summary: This research explores perspective latents as an architectural condition for causal emergence in active inference agents. It investigates how reward-free predictive organization relates to causal emergence in active inference.

title: LLMs Get Lost in Evolving User Intent
summary: This research highlights that large language models (LLMs), when deployed as collaborative agents, struggle with handling evolving user intent during iterative interactions. It points out that users dynamically shape their intent, which current LLMs find challenging to follow.

title: Cardinality-Decomposed Loss: Matching Training Objectives to Relation Structure in Heterogeneous Recommendation Graphs
summary: This research introduces a "Cardinality-Decomposed Loss" function for training Graph Neural Networks on heterogeneous recommendation graphs. It aims to better match training objectives to the varying cardinality of relations within these graphs.

title: Adaptive Confidence-weighted Expansion for Trustworthy Multi-Omics Multimodal Fusion
summary: This research proposes an "Adaptive Confidence-weighted Expansion" method for trustworthy multi-omics multimodal fusion, particularly for medical prognosis. It aims to improve model performance and reliability when dealing with noisy or uninformative data streams.

title: GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries
summary: GaugeQuant introduces a method for online learning of quantization-optimal bases from LLM symmetries. It leverages internal continuous symmetries in Transformers during training to minimize activation outliers for more efficient quantization.

title: Toward Mechanistic Interpretability of an AI Foundation Model Fine-Tuned for Atmospheric Chemistry
summary: This research explores the mechanistic interpretability of an AI foundation model fine-tuned for atmospheric chemistry and air quality prediction. It aims to understand how these models generate forecasts, offering insights into their internal workings.

title: Memoir: Should a Model Write to Its Memory While It Thinks?
summary: Memoir is a system that combines per-sample fast memory with shared slow parameters and variable-depth latent recurrence, designed with a future-latent energy objective. It investigates the dynamics of a model writing to its memory during an iterative thinking process.

title: New Complexity-Theoretic Frontiers of Tractability for Neural Network Training
summary: This paper explores the computational complexity and tractability of optimally training neural networks, addressing a fundamental theoretical gap in machine learning research.

title: Robust Asynchronous Q-Learning under Reward and State Corruption via Batching
summary: This research introduces a method for robust asynchronous Q-learning that can learn an optimal policy even when reward and state observations are adversarially corrupted.

title: What is Good? Extracting and Testing Implicit Theories of Literary Quality from LLM Reasoning Traces
summary: This study investigates how reasoning-enabled large language models (LLMs) evaluate literary quality and presents a benchmark of real texts to test these implicit theories.

title: Knowledge Injection Exists in MoE? Exploring Expert-Aware Contrast Decoding in MoE for Mitigating LLMs'Hallucinations
summary: This paper proposes an 'Expert-Aware Contrast Decoding' method for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models to mitigate hallucinations in large language models by leveraging layer-wise differences.

title: Is MoE Routing a Huffman Code? Discovering the Frequency-Diversity Law in Chain-of-Thought
summary: This research uncovers a fundamental principle of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing, suggesting it functions as a manifestation of Huffman Coding and introducing the Frequency-Diversity Law.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model Framework for Identification of Cutaneous Immune-Related Adverse Events
summary: This study evaluates a human-in-the-loop framework using retrieval-augmented, multi-agent large language models for accurately detecting cutaneous immune-related adverse events from clinical notes.

title: More Is Not More: What Matters for Diversity in LLM Opinions?
summary: This paper investigates the problem of opinion homogenization in large language model outputs when simulating human opinions and explores interventions to increase diversity.

title: LLM-INSTRUCT at UZH Shared Task 2026: Constraint-Aware Retrieval and Selective Debate for Paragraph-Level Argument Mining
summary: This article describes LLM-INSTRUCT, the winning system for the UZH Shared Task at ArgMining 2026, which performs paragraph-level argument mining using constraint-aware retrieval and selective debate.

title: Skill-Contracted Agents for Evidence-Aware Materials Literature Analysis
summary: This work introduces 'Skill-Contracted Agents' designed for evidence-aware materials literature analysis, addressing the limitations of conventional RAG pipelines in handling heterogeneous tasks.

title: Position: Natural Language Should Not Fully Replace Formal Languages
summary: This position paper argues against the claim that natural language should entirely replace formal languages in areas like software design, highlighting overlooked fundamental linguistic properties.

title: Moir: Let the Model Direct Its Own Story for Robust Cross-Domain Knowledge Editing
summary: This paper introduces 'Moir,' a method enabling language models to direct their own story for robust cross-domain knowledge editing, aiming to prevent the erosion of core capabilities.

title: Break Through the Compression Bottleneck: From Theory to Practice
summary: This paper addresses the 'compression bottleneck' in large language models, exploring methods to effectively reduce computational and memory overhead without significant performance degradation.

title: Making Open-Source Text LLM Watermarks Durable Against Merging
summary: This research focuses on making open-source text LLM watermarks durable against post-training modifications like model merging, which typically remove existing watermarks.

title: Routing Subspaces: Auditing Evaluation-to-Deployment Mismatch in Fine-Tuned Language Models
summary: This paper examines the 'evaluation-to-deployment mismatch' in fine-tuned language models, where safety evaluations may not accurately reflect behavior in ordinary use.

title: TopoGuard: Graph Theory Based Defenses Against Split-Knowledge Attacks on RAG
summary: This paper introduces 'TopoGuard,' a graph theory-based defense mechanism to protect Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems from split-knowledge attacks involving injected adversarial documents.

title: Preference Tuning as Spectral Update Reorganization
summary: This research investigates preference-based post-training methods like RLHF by analyzing the spectral structure of their induced parameter updates, offering insights into how models learn from preferences.

title: AsymVerify at SemEval-2026 Task 6: Asymmetric Confidence-Gated Verification for Political Evasion Detection
summary: This article presents AsymVerify, a confidence-gated verification system for the SemEval-2026 Task 6, focusing on the challenging task of detecting political evasion in responses.

title: Answer-then-Edit: Reasoning Skeleton Editing for Anti-Distillation with Preserved Utility
summary: This paper introduces 'Answer-then-Edit,' a method for reasoning skeleton editing aimed at anti-distillation to protect proprietary large language models from unauthorized knowledge extraction.

title: Belief Propagation in LLM World Models: Measuring Strategic Information Bias with Prediction Markets
summary: This research demonstrates how large language models combined with prediction markets can serve as a calibrated instrument for measuring strategic information bias within information ecosystems.

title: Naver-News-KO: A Korean News Summarization Dataset for Open-Source Fine-Tuning of Summarization Models
summary: This paper announces the release of Naver-News-KO, a new Korean news summarization dataset consisting of 27,400 document-summary pairs for fine-tuning and evaluating summarization models.

title: GLAN-QnA-KR: A Seedless Taxonomy-Driven Korean Instruction Corpus
summary: This paper introduces GLAN-QnA-KR, a 303,581-row openly redistributable Korean instruction-QA corpus, generated using a seedless taxonomy-driven pipeline with Microsoft's Phi-3.5-MoE-instruct. The corpus aims to provide a resource for AI development, particularly for instruction following.

title: Confidently Deceptive: How Confidence Amplifies the Risk of LLM Deception
summary: This research investigates how large language models (LLMs) produce deceptive responses and explores whether the models' confidence in these deceptions amplifies their persuasiveness to users. The study examines the ethical implications of LLM deception.

title: SCoPE: Shift-Aware Speaker-Conditioned Priors for Emotion Recognition in Conversations
summary: This paper introduces SCoPE, a system designed for emotion recognition in conversations that incorporates shift-aware speaker-conditioned priors to account for the transient and speaker-specific evolution of emotions. The method aims to improve the tracking of emotional changes across utterances.

title: Distinguishing Artificial from Authentic: Evaluating LLMs for Detecting LLM-Generated Content
summary: This research evaluates the capability of large language models (LLMs) to distinguish between AI-generated and human-authored content, focusing on its application for detecting AI-generated responses and code in academic settings. The study investigates the extent to which LLMs can serve as effective detectors.

title: thaulab@EEUCA 2026: Who Said What to Whom? A Targeting-Aware Neural-Symbolic Pipeline for Gaming Toxicity Detection
summary: This paper presents a three-stage neural-symbolic pipeline for detecting toxicity in gaming chat, developed for the EEUCA 2026 Shared Task. The system combines an ensemble of compact transformers with a Linguistically-Informed Mediator to address toxicity classification.

title: Domyn-Small: A European 10B Reasoning Language Model
summary: Domyn-Small is introduced as a new 10-billion-parameter open-weight reasoning language model, released under the MIT license. It was pre-trained on 9 trillion tokens of multilingual data and subsequently post-trained for reasoning and instruction following.

title: The Storyteller in the Model: Narrative Pattern Inheritance, Escalation Dynamics, and Alignment Governance in LLMs
summary: This paper examines how narrative patterns embedded in the training data of large language models (LLMs) influence their behavior, leading to potential systematic behavioral influences and governance risks. It investigates the implications for LLM alignment and safety.

title: ShriNep@EEUCA 2026: RAKSHAK - Multi-Task DeBERTa with Rationale Distillation and Jigsaw-Augmented Training for Toxic Intent Classification
summary: This paper presents two systems, including RAKSHAK, for the GameTox Shared Task on toxic intent classification in World of Tanks chat. The systems utilize multi-task DeBERTa with rationale distillation and jigsaw-augmented training.

title: Semantic Field Theory: Historical Origin, Higher-Order Interaction, and Stabilized Semantic Inference
summary: This paper reconstructs the historical evolution of Semantic Field Theory (SFT), tracing its development from a philosophical critique to a proposed computational model class for lexical semantics, higher-order composition, and stabilized interpretation. It aims to clarify SFT's theoretical foundations and applications.

title: A Knowledge-Injection Framework for Zero-Shot Adaptation of LLMs to Delirium Prediction
summary: This paper presents a lightweight knowledge-injection framework designed for the zero-shot adaptation of large language models (LLMs) to ICU delirium prediction. The framework aims to enhance LLMs' performance on specialized clinical tasks by addressing domain knowledge limitations.

title: Response drift across frontier large language models
summary: This research systematically evaluates "response drift" across frontier large language models (LLMs), where outputs deviate from expert-validated references. It quantifies the magnitude and structure of this drift through a fully crossed human evaluation.

title: RE-AD: Real-Time Requirement Adherence for Data Labeling
summary: This paper introduces RE-AD (Real-Time Requirement Adherence), a framework designed to improve the quality of human-annotated data for large language models. The system addresses common issues in crowd-sourced annotations, such as misunderstanding or lack of engagement.

title: Learn2Zinc: Fine-tuning Small Language Models for Text-to-Model Translation in MiniZinc
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of fine-tuning small language models (0.6B to 20B parameters) for text-to-model translation in domain-specific languages like MiniZinc. The study aims to improve code generation for such languages where larger models often struggle.

title: Dropping the Anchor: Statistical Context Summarization for Distributed Systems via Pulsar Attention
summary: This paper proposes "Pulsar Attention" for statistical context summarization in distributed systems, a method designed to reduce the computational cost of large language model (LLM) inference on long sequences by addressing the quadratic complexity of self-attention.

title: CAMeR: Keyword-Gated Hybrid Activation for Adaptive Memory Retention in LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces CAMeR (Contextual Adaptive Memory Retention), a keyword-gated hybrid activation memory system for LLM agents. CAMeR adaptively retains relevant information and distinguishes it from irrelevant knowledge during extended dialogues.

title: Instruct-FD: Can Your Full-Duplex Speech System Follow Turn-Taking Instructions?
summary: This research investigates the ability of full-duplex (FD) spoken dialogue systems to adapt their turn-taking behavior when given explicit instructions. The study highlights the importance of this capability for real-world deployment where conversational policies vary.

title: Can Valence Reflect Morality in Natural Language? A Preliminary Annotation Study
summary: This preliminary annotation study explores whether valence, representing feelings or affect, can reflect morality in natural language, aiming to investigate if AI behavior can mirror virtuous human ethical conduct. The research contributes to understanding AI ethics.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Persona Simulation in Opinion Prediction with GPT-4.1
summary: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of persona simulation using large language models, specifically GPT-4.1, for predicting opinions. The study explores the current limitations and future directions of this technique in anticipating human choices.

title: Frontier Financial Judgement: Can agents tell what might move a stock?
summary: This paper introduces "Frontier Financial Judgement," a new benchmark co-developed with professional equity analysts. It assesses AI agents' ability to replicate expert human judgments in financial analysis, including identifying new information and evaluating its valuation impact on stocks.

title: Learning to Detect UI Principle Violations via Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research explores the use of reinforcement learning to detect violations of established UI quality principles in web front-end code generated by small language models and coding agents. It aims to evaluate the quality of AI-generated interfaces beyond functional correctness.

title: REGARD: Regional Affective Differences in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates regional affective differences in Large Language Models (LLMs), examining how models trained in different linguistic and regional contexts frame political, cultural, and geopolitical entities, often evaluated through sentiment or favorability.

title: Rushes: A Human Preference Dataset for Pluralistic Alignment
summary: This introduces Rushes, a dataset and benchmark designed to study human engagement preferences within interactive AI-generated narrative environments, collected through a game interface.

title: Are Diversity Metrics Measuring Diversity? A Capability-Controlled Audit of Majority-Vote Gain in LLM Ensembles
summary: This study audits five diversity metrics used for LLM ensembles, questioning whether they accurately measure diversity or primarily reflect model capability, by tracking their prediction of majority-vote gain.

title: The Geometry of Personality: Activation Steering with Jungian Cognitive Functions
summary: This research explores using Jungian Cognitive Functions with activation steering to control and interpret personality in Large Language Models, moving beyond static trait frameworks.

title: REFACT: Adaptive Fact Restatement for Compact and Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes REFACT, an adaptive fact restatement method designed to improve the faithfulness and compactness of Chain-of-Thought reasoning in Large Language Models, especially when evidence is sparse or conflicting.

title: CSPF: A Constrained Shared-Private Fusion Method for Non-Verifiable Preference Evaluation
summary: This work introduces CSPF (Constrained Shared-Private Fusion), a novel fusion method aimed at reliably evaluating non-verifiable tasks by better capturing the diverse human evaluative criteria.

title: LegalCiteTrust: Benchmarking Citation Trustworthiness in Chinese Long-Form Legal Research Reports
summary: LegalCiteTrust is introduced as a benchmark for assessing the trustworthiness of citations in Chinese long-form legal research reports generated by LLMs and agentic systems, focusing on the reliability of legal authorities.

title: Tencent WorkBuddy Bench: A Multi-Domain Coding-Agent Benchmark with Contamination-Resistant Task Construction
summary: Tencent WorkBuddy Bench is presented as a multi-domain evaluation suite for coding agents, detailing its construction methodology, scoring protocol, and a cross-model leaderboard.

title: Where Animacy Lives in Large Language Models: Tracing the Circuits of the Animacy Concept
summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models distinguish animate from inanimate concepts, tracing the internal circuits to understand their representation of animacy.

title: CultureTalk-ID: A Multi-Task Dialogue Benchmark for Cultural Commonsense in Indonesian Local Languages
summary: CultureTalk-ID is introduced as the first dialogue-based benchmark designed to evaluate cultural commonsense in Large Language Models for Indonesian local languages, addressing limitations of isolated prompts.

title: Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience
summary: This paper explores sample-efficient learning for agents by leveraging in-context learning from their own interaction histories, which is crucial when real-world environment interactions are costly.

title: QuantiBias: Benchmarking Quantization-Induced Bias in LLMs
summary: QuantiBias is presented as a method for benchmarking the increased bias induced in Large Language Models by quantization, a side effect often missed by standard safety evaluations.

title: PrefReward: Learning User Preference Matrix for Personalized Text Generation
summary: This paper introduces PrefReward, a method for learning user preference matrices to enable more personalized text generation by Large Language Models, moving beyond implicit preference representations.

title: One More Turn, Less Regret: A Regret-Based Multi-Turn Benchmark for LLMs' Clarification Policies
summary: RegretBench is introduced as a regret-based, multi-turn benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models' clarification policies as sequential decision problems when faced with ambiguous user requests.

title: Progressive Cramming: Reliable Token Compression and What It Reveals
summary: This work introduces progressive cramming, a method for reliable token compression into learned embeddings with near-perfect reconstruction, revealing insights into fundamental limits and optimization challenges.

title: slang.gr as a Large-Scale Crowdsourced Resource for Non-Standard Greek
summary: This study presents slang.gr as a large-scale crowdsourced resource for non-standard Greek, offering the first large-scale computational study of this linguistic data for modeling slang.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Embeddings and LLMs in a Greek Book Publisher Setting - The CUP Dataset
summary: This paper introduces CUP, a Greek book retrieval benchmark consisting of catalog records and expert-annotated queries, to comparatively evaluate sparse, dense, hybrid, and LLM-assisted retrieval methods.

title: A Unified Moral-Value Dataset for Instruction Tuning
summary: This work introduces a unified moral-value dataset for instruction tuning, aiming to effectively align Large Language Models with specific human values.

title: news-crawler-LM: A Small Long-Context Model For High-Quality News Crawling
summary: This introduces news-crawler-LM, a small, long-context model specifically designed for high-quality news crawling by extracting structured content from diverse and complex news page layouts.

title: RealVDeblur: One-Step Diffusion for Generalizable Real-World Video Deblurring
summary: This work presents RealVDeblur, an efficient one-step diffusion model for generalizable real-world video deblurring, addressing challenges like diverse motion patterns and complex degradations.

title: Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion
summary: Introduces Axolotl3D, a unified framework for faithful 3D shape completion that addresses limitations of existing 3D generative models in multi-view or occluded scenarios.

title: ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs
summary: Presents ODeform, a new method that uses Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to learn continuous 4D motion for shape deformation, relevant for computer vision and robotics tasks.

title: Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
summary: Discusses the development of Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models to improve the trustworthiness and interpretability of AI predictions for breast ultrasound diagnosis in medical imaging.

title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmed GANs 2026: Geometric Filtering for Privacy-Preserving CT Slice Generation
summary: Introduces a privacy-preserving framework utilizing geometric filtering for synthetic lung CT slice generation, developed for the Image-CLEFmed GANs 2026 challenge.

title: U-CFR: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement for Interactive Segmentation
summary: Proposes U-CFR (Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement), a novel inference-time framework to improve interactive image segmentation by reducing the need for corrective clicks.

title: Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness
summary: This research rethinks Open-World Video Anomaly Detection (OWVAD), diagnosing a limitation called "definition blindness" where models struggle to adapt to user-specified anomaly definitions.

title: 3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch
summary: Introduces 3D-GIMP, a method for 3D scene editing that combines 3D Gaussian Inpainting with PatchMatch to improve detail and reduce multi-view inconsistencies compared to iterative diffusion models.

title: Ocular Verification for Virtual Reality
summary: Explores methods for ocular verification, such as iris recognition, for user authentication within virtual reality (VR) headsets, addressing limitations of traditional approaches.

title: Explainable graph attention network for stress recognition (StressGAT) via differential action units
summary: Presents StressGAT, an explainable graph attention network designed for stress recognition based on differential action units from facial expressions, aiming to address individual variability.

title: Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation
summary: Introduces "Agentic Designer," a system that uses progressive multi-agent collaboration to generate realistic interior furniture layouts that adhere to architectural constraints.

title: ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?
summary: Introduces ViSTR-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to reason from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes.

title: Webly Supervised Multi-Label Recognition: Evaluation Benchmark and Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning
summary: Presents an evaluation benchmark and a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning method to advance webly supervised multi-label recognition, addressing the current lack of unified evaluation.

title: Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting
summary: Introduces Lumera, a method for engine-native editable 3D world reconstruction from single images, providing object instances and lights that can be imported into standard engines.

title: DINO-VPT: Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning for Joint Physical-Digital Face Anti-Spoofing
summary: Presents DINO-VPT, a method using Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning to create unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) models capable of detecting both physical and digital spoofing attacks.

title: Sidewalk Moments: Are Richer Representations Always More Human-Aligned? Evidence from City-Walk Videos
summary: This research investigates whether richer visual representations from city-walk videos lead to more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, using a dataset of 61 first-person videos.

title: FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head
summary: Proposes FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model, for one-shot creation of animatable 4D Gaussian heads, also enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery.

title: MagicMakeup: A Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for High-Fidelity Makeup-Transfer
summary: Introduces MagicMakeup, a Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for high-fidelity makeup transfer that preserves identity while allowing precise regional editing on faces.

title: Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention
summary: Presents Ms. Forcing, a method for efficient streaming video generation that uses multi-scale patchification and attention to overcome the real-time deployment challenges of current diffusion models.

title: RECO: Region-Aware Compensation for Extrinsic Perturbations in Roadside 3D Detection
summary: Introduces RECO, a method for Region-Aware Compensation designed to mitigate the effects of extrinsic perturbations on roadside 3D object detection, improving perception for autonomous driving.

title: FSB-Net: Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network for Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Non-Contrast CT
summary: Proposes FSB-Net (Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network), a new model for accurate segmentation of brain stroke lesions in challenging non-contrast CT scans.

title: Unsupervised Metal Artifact Reduction in Dental CBCT using Fine-tuned Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
summary: This paper proposes an unsupervised deep learning framework using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks for reducing metal artifacts in dental cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. This method aims to improve diagnostic precision by obscuring anatomical structures.

title: Distribution-Alignment Bridge for Uncertainty-Aware Text-to-Video Retrieval
summary: This paper introduces the Distribution-Alignment Bridge (DAB), a framework that reframes text-to-video retrieval as a distribution alignment task. It models text and video embeddings as Gaussian distributions to enhance uncertainty-aware retrieval.

title: HyWorldVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Hybrid World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper presents HyWorldVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model featuring hybrid world modeling designed for end-to-end autonomous driving. The model aims to balance fine-grained spatiotemporal reasoning with robustness in noisy driving scenarios.

title: Latent Variable-Mediated Cross-Learning for Few-Shot Acoustic Impedance Imaging
summary: This research proposes a latent variable-mediated cross-learning approach for few-shot acoustic impedance imaging, a challenging problem in subsurface analysis. The method addresses issues like unknown seismic wavelets and scarce labeled data in this domain.

title: Sparse Concept Channels in Frozen 3D CT Vision Encoders
summary: This study investigates sparse concept channels within frozen 3D CT vision encoders, aiming to understand how large vision-language models encode clinical findings in their internal representations for medical image interpretation.

title: ProCap: Prominence-guided Object Rectification for Faithful and Comprehensive Video Captioning
summary: ProCap introduces a prominence-guided object rectification method to improve video captioning quality by grounding captions in detected objects. This training-free approach aims to reduce hallucination and provide more faithful and comprehensive video descriptions.

title: GroupVideo: Multi-Identity Customized Text-to-Video Generation
summary: GroupVideo proposes a new method for multi-identity customized text-to-video generation, aiming to overcome identity confusion in multi-person scenarios. It focuses on explicit identity separation mechanisms to improve generation quality.

title: GeoThreat: Transferable Targeted Adversarial Attacks on Large Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing Image Interpretation
summary: GeoThreat introduces transferable targeted adversarial attacks designed to assess the robustness of large vision-language models (LVLMs) in interpreting remote sensing imagery. This research aims to identify vulnerabilities in their cross-modal semantic understanding.

title: HyperImageNet: A Large-Scale High-Spatial Resolution Hyperspectral Imagery Classification Benchmark
summary: HyperImageNet is presented as a large-scale benchmark dataset for fine-grained hyperspectral land-cover understanding. It comprises 26,084 airborne hyperspectral image patches with 224 spectral bands and 138 land-cover categories.

title: Achieving Text-based Person Retrieval with Any Granularity
summary: This paper introduces a new paradigm and systematic solution for text-based person retrieval that addresses the challenge of query granularity uncertainty. It formalizes a five-level granularity hierarchy to handle diverse retrieval scenarios.

title: MVEI & EmObserver: Empowering MLLM-Oriented Visual Emotional Intelligence via Emotion Statement Judgement
summary: This research introduces MVEI & EmObserver, a framework designed to empower and systematically evaluate the visual emotional intelligence of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It focuses on emotion statement judgment within Affective Image Content Analysis.

title: Do Pathology Vision-Language Models Truly See Pathology?
summary: This paper critically examines pathology vision-language models (VLMs), questioning if they truly understand pathology or rely on superficial cues. It identifies overlooked issues in current VQA benchmarks, such as visual evidence not always being necessary for accurate answers.

title: TransBiolab: A Real-World Multi-View Dataset of Cluttered Transparent Biomedical Objects
summary: TransBiolab is introduced as a new real-world, multi-view dataset containing cluttered transparent biomedical objects. It aims to address the scarcity of high-quality data for autonomous visual perception and manipulation in biomedical laboratories.

title: Show, Don't Tell: Evaluating Spatial Cognition in Generative Pixels Rather Than LLM Text
summary: This paper proposes a novel method for evaluating spatial cognition in AI agents by generating pixels rather than relying on LLM text. This approach aims to better assess agents' spatial intelligence in continuous visual scenes for physical world interaction.

title: C-PTQ: Fisher-weighted Channel-wise Sensitivity for Post-training Quantization of MLLMs
summary: C-PTQ introduces Fisher-weighted channel-wise sensitivity for post-training quantization (PTQ) of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). This method aims to efficiently compress models and accelerate inference while mitigating performance degradation.

title: Geo3R: Mitigating Spatial Reasoning Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Geo3R proposes a method to mitigate spatial reasoning hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It aims to prevent models from producing judgments that contradict the true 3D structure of a scene.

title: Loss Landscape Topology Reveals Why Simple Baselines are Competitive at 3D Point Cloud Segmentation Under Class Imbalance
summary: This research analyzes loss landscape topology to explain why simple baseline methods are competitive for 3D point cloud segmentation under class imbalance. It systematically evaluates 11 imbalance mitigation approaches across various datasets.

title: HalluScope: Fine-grained Hallucination Diagnosis for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: HalluScope introduces a fine-grained diagnosis method for hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It helps identify inconsistencies in model outputs related to visual content, textual context, or commonsense knowledge.

title: Safety-oriented sidewalk and road segmentation for smartphone-based assistive navigation
summary: This study presents a safety-oriented semantic segmentation framework for smartphone-based assistive navigation, designed to distinguish walkable sidewalks from unsafe regions. It aims to improve independent sidewalk mobility for blind and visually impaired pedestrians.

title: DTIF: Robust Loop Closure Detection via Delaunay Triangle Topology in Complex Forests
summary: DTIF proposes a robust loop closure detection method using Delaunay Triangle Topology for accurate forest inventory and large-scale mapping. This method is particularly effective in GNSS-denied understory environments.

title: CRAG-MM-Diagnostics: Enabling Stage-Wise Analysis of Knowledge-Intensive VQA
summary: This paper introduces CRAG-MM-Diagnostics, a new benchmark designed for stage-wise analysis of Knowledge-Intensive Visual Question Answering (KI-VQA). It evaluates Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on their ability to act as multimodal knowledge assistants, requiring external information beyond an image.

title: Decoupling Cross-Modality Manifold Discrepancy: Leveraging Visible Diffusion Priors for Infrared Super-Resolution
summary: This research proposes a method for infrared image super-resolution (IISR) that leverages visible diffusion priors to improve image clarity. It aims to decouple cross-modality manifold discrepancy while preserving structural information in low-resolution infrared images.

title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
summary: This paper explores token compression techniques for Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) to reduce input token cost during inference. The research addresses the high cost of visual tokens when Omni-LLMs process audio, video, and text jointly.

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning Model for Cross-Modality Super-Resolution in Fluorescence Microscopy
summary: This research introduces a physics-informed deep learning model for cross-modality super-resolution in fluorescence microscopy. The model aims to generate high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while ensuring consistency with optical image formation principles.

title: Learning-based Seam Correspondence Reconstruction in Sewing Patterns
summary: This paper presents a graph-based learning framework for reconstructing two-level stitching information in digital sewing patterns. The method aims to automate seam correspondence reconstruction, which is crucial for 3D modeling and typically requires labor-intensive expert specification.

title: DART: A Degradation-Aware Recurrent Transformer for Archival Film Restoration
summary: This research introduces DART, a Degradation-Aware Recurrent Transformer, for archival film restoration. The model addresses compound degradations in historical footage like scratches, blur, and flicker, without relying on clean reference videos.

title: Stokes-Informed Diffusion for Robust Linear Polarization Estimation
summary: This research proposes a Stokes-Informed Diffusion method for robust linear polarization estimation from a single RGB image. The technique aims to extract polarization cues, useful for applications like material detection, without requiring dedicated hardware.

title: HERMES: Heterogeneous Edge-Relational Multi-Head Embedded SSM Attention for Traffic Conflict Prediction at Signalized Intersections
summary: This paper introduces HERMES, a Heterogeneous Edge-Relational Multi-Head Embedded SSM Attention model, for predicting traffic conflicts at signalized intersections. The method aims to better represent complex multi-agent interactions for proactive traffic safety assessment.

title: PhysCoRe: Physics-Corrected Residual World Models for Material-Aware Deformable Dynamics
summary: This research presents PhysCoRe, Physics-Corrected Residual World Models, to predict the dynamics of deformable objects during robotic manipulation. The model aims to improve generalization and accuracy by incorporating physical corrections into learned material-aware dynamics.

title: Scalable Low-Cost Laboratory Automation: A Digital Twin-Integrated Robotic Platform for Autonomous Liquid Handling (RAINBOTTM)
summary: This work introduces RAINBOT™, a low-cost, openly reproducible robotic platform integrated with a digital twin for autonomous liquid handling in laboratories. The system aims to address the high cost and proprietary nature of commercial lab automation.

title: Safe and Scalable Multi-Drone Payload Transport via CBF-based Reinforcement Learning with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
